definition_zh: 护照；通行证；途径
definition_en: an official document that identifies you and lets you travel abroad; also a permit to pass through a place, or something that opens the way to an opportunity
core_image: 一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次放行
scene: 机场的查验台前排着长队，旅客把证件从包里拿出来，等着印章落下。She handed her passport to the officer and waited for the stamp.
sceneCN: 这里是「护照」（第 1 个义项：出入国境时证明身份的官方证件）；句意是她把护照递给工作人员，等对方盖章放行。画面里可想到查验台、行李牌与印章。

derivatives.zh: 由 passport 与 control 复合而成，指边境对护照的查验环节
由 passport 与 photo 复合而成，指用于护照的证件照
由 passport 与表示「持有者」的 holder 复合而成，指护照持有人

senses.title: An official document for travelling abroad
senses.definition: an official document issued by a government that identifies you and allows you to travel to other countries
senses.definitionCN: 由政府签发、证明身份并允许你前往他国旅行的官方证件
senses.example: My passport expires next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我的护照明年春天到期。
senses.why: The word joins passing and a port: the paper that once let a traveller through a harbour gate became the paper that lets a person cross a border.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「通过」与「港口」拼在一起：最初让旅客通过港口关卡的文书，后来成了让人跨越国境的证件。

senses.title: A permit to pass through a place
senses.titleCN: 通行证；通过某地的许可
senses.definition: an official paper allowing a person or a ship to enter, leave or move through a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 准许某人或某船进出、通过某地的官方文书
senses.example: In the old harbour, no ship sailed without a passport from the governor.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的港口，没有总督签发的通行证，任何船都不能出海。
senses.why: Before modern borders existed, a passport was aimed at a gate or a harbour rather than at a country, and history books still use the word that way.
senses.whyCN: 在现代国界形成之前，passport 针对的是一道关口或一个港口，而不是整个国家，历史叙述里至今保留这层用法。

senses.title: A means of reaching something
senses.definition: something that makes it possible for you to go somewhere or to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 使你得以进入某地或取得某种成就的东西
senses.example: A good command of English is a passport to better jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的英语能力是获得更好工作的敲门砖。
senses.why: If a passport opens a border, then any paper, skill or contact that opens a door can borrow the name, because the movement from document to opportunity is the same.
senses.whyCN: 既然护照能打开国界，那么任何能打开一道门的证书、技能或人脉都可以借用这个称呼，因为「从证件到机会」的这一步是相同的。

intro.en: Passport fuses a verb of stepping with the Latin word for a harbour, and the paper it names has kept that gate-opening picture for six centuries.
intro.cn: passport 把表示「迈步」的动词与拉丁语里的「港口」合在一起，这个证件名称也因此把「打开关口」的画面保留了六百多年。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, naming the ground a foot could cover in one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的地面。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday speech, and a compound of passer with port named a paper for passing a port.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常语言，passer 与 port 组成的复合词则指准许通过港口的文书。

items.en: Medieval Italian passaporto recorded the same compound for a document that let a ship or a person leave a port, and French passed the form on to English.
items.cn: 中古意大利语 passaporto 记录了同样的复合词，指让船只或人员离开港口的文书，法语又把这一形式传给了英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the travel document as the main sense and extends the word to anything that opens a way, from a skill to a good name.
items.cn: 现代英语以出入境证件为主要义项，并把词义扩展到任何能打开通路的东西，从一门技能到好名声。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the stepping verb or on the harbour noun; the near-meaning group collects papers that grant entry or permission.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在「迈步」动词或「港口」名词上的词；近义组收的是准许入境或授予许可的证件。

entries.definition: To go past a point, or to hand something to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某一点；也指把东西递给别人。

entries.definition: A way through, or a section of a text or a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指文章的一段或旅程的一段。

entries.definition: A person who happens to be walking past.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好从旁边走过的路人。

entries.definition: Out of date; no longer fashionable.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的；不再时髦的。

entries.definition: An official mark or sticker in a passport allowing entry to a country.
entries.definitionCN: 护照上准许进入某国的官方签注或贴纸。

entries.definition: An official document giving permission to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 准许做某事的官方文件。

entries.definition: A paper or file that records information and can prove identity.
entries.definitionCN: 记录信息、可用以证明身份的纸张或文件。

normalIntro.en: The word is a small machine of two parts: a verb for stepping and a noun for a harbour, locked together into one paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两部分咬合成一台小机器：一个表示迈步的动词，一个表示港口的名词，合成同一张纸。

normal.en: Pass means to go by, and port means a harbour, so a passport is literally a paper for going through a port.
normal.cn: pass 意为经过，port 意为港口，所以 passport 字面上就是「通过港口的纸」。

normal.en: Airports still keep the old picture alive: passport control stands exactly where a gate would be.
normal.cn: 机场仍在延续这个旧画面：护照查验处就设在相当于关口的位置。

normal.en: The plural is regular, passports, because it is an ordinary countable noun.
normal.cn: 复数按规则加 s 写作 passports，因为它就是普通的可数名词。

normal.en: The phrase a passport to success shows how a document for borders turned into a word for opportunity.
normal.cn: a passport to success 这个说法显示出：一张管边界的证件如何变成了表示机会的词。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable, so the two parts are spoken as one word rather than as pass and port.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音节，因此两个部分读起来是一个词，而不是分开的 pass 与 port。

abstract.en: A passport is a state promising, in ink and paper, that you may be let through.
abstract.cn: 护照是国家用油墨和纸张作出的承诺：你可以被放行。

abstract.en: Every border turns a small book into a key, which is why the same word can later mean any key.
abstract.cn: 每一道国界都会把一本小册子变成钥匙，所以这个词后来能指任何一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that permission is a thing you can hold in your hand and lose in a minute.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：许可是可以握在手里、也能在一分钟内丢掉的东西。

examples.en: She showed her passport at the desk and was waved through.
examples.cn: 她在柜台出示护照，随即被示意通过。

examples.en: A second language can be a passport to work in another country.
examples.cn: 第二门语言可以成为到别国工作的途径。

examples.en: The old rule required every vessel to carry a passport from the port authority.
examples.cn: 旧时的规定要求每艘船都携带港务当局签发的通行证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死跑特」——出门在外最怕丢了它，还得赶紧跑；passport 就是护照。

root: 由古法语 passer（经过）与 port（港口）复合，源头可追到拉丁语 passus（一步）与 portus（港口）；本义是准许通过港口的文书。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a paper that opens a gate; the senses run from the travel document to the older harbour permit and then to any means of access.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一张能打开关口的纸；义项从出入境证件，到较早的港口通行许可，再到任何通往机会的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dark booklet handed through a window in exchange for a nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次点头放行。

branches.en: a queue at a border desk in the early morning
branches.cn: 清晨边检柜台前的一条长队

branches.en: a ship waiting for a stamped paper before it sails
branches.cn: 一条等着盖章文书才敢出海的船

branches.en: a language certificate placed on a job application
branches.cn: 一份语言证书放在求职材料上

branches.en: the same paper serving a traveller and a vessel
branches.cn: 同一张纸先后服务于旅客与船只

branches.en: a gate that opens first for a ship and later for a career
branches.cn: 先是向船只、后是向职业打开的一道门

intro.en: Two Latin pieces hold the word together: a noun for a step with its verb, and a noun for a harbour that English still uses on its own.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分撑起这个词：一个表示脚步的名词及其动词，一个表示港口的名词，后者英语至今单独使用。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a paper allowing passage through a port

definition_zh: 畜牧的；牧羊的；田园的；牧歌式的；牧师的；田园诗
definition_en: relating to shepherds or country life, or to the care of a religious congregation
core_image: 一道石墙围着草坡，羊群散在墙内，墙外的城市只剩一条模糊的边
scene: 清晨的坡地上羊群散开，A pastoral valley keeps its shepherds and its dry stone walls.
sceneCN: 这里 pastoral 指「与牧羊、畜牧相关的」（第 1 个义项：畜牧的）；句意为这座牧歌式的山谷仍保留着牧人与干砌石墙。图中可辨识物件：干砌石墙、羊群、牧杖、远处城市的轮廓。

pos.zh: 畜牧的；田园的；牧歌式的；牧灵的

derivatives.zh: 牧师；牧人
牧场；放牧
畜牧主义；畜牧生活
畜牧者

senses.title: Relating to sheep and cattle farming
senses.definition: concerned with the grazing of livestock rather than with crops
senses.definitionCN: 与放牧牲畜有关，而非与种植作物有关
senses.example: Pastoral land here is too dry for wheat and too steep for ploughs.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的牧地太干种不了麦，太陡使不了犁。
senses.why: pastor is Latin for shepherd, so the first sense is the working sense: everything to do with grazing animals.
senses.whyCN: pastor 是拉丁语「牧人」，因此第一个义项是干活的义：一切与放牧牲畜有关的事。

senses.title: An idealised countryside
senses.definition: describing a peaceful rural scene imagined as simple and harmonious
senses.definitionCN: 形容被想象为朴素和谐的宁静乡野景象
senses.example: The brochure sells a pastoral image of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 宣传册贩卖一种田园式的乡村生活形象。
senses.why: town writers looked at herding country and saw peace, so the working word acquired a glow it did not have for the herders.
senses.whyCN: 城里的写作者看着牧区，看到了安宁，于是这个干活用的词多了一层牧人自己感受不到的光晕。

senses.title: A literary and artistic mode
senses.titleCN: 文学与艺术中的牧歌体裁
senses.definition: belonging to poems, plays, music or paintings that treat shepherd life as a theme
senses.definitionCN: 属于以牧人生活为主题的诗歌、戏剧、音乐或绘画
senses.example: The pastoral tradition puts shepherds into a golden weather that never rains.
senses.exampleCN: 牧歌传统把牧人放进一个从不下雨的金色天气里。
senses.why: the idealised countryside became a genre with set conventions, and the adjective names the genre.
senses.whyCN: 理想化的乡野变成有固定套路的体裁，形容词便用来命名这一体裁。

senses.title: Care of a congregation
senses.definition: in religion, relating to the guidance and care a minister gives to people
senses.definitionCN: 宗教中指牧师对人所给予的引导与照顾
senses.example: Pastoral care includes visiting the sick and the lonely.
senses.exampleCN: 牧灵关怀包括探访病人与孤独者。
senses.why: the Latin shepherd was applied to clergy, so the same adjective covers looking after a flock of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「牧人」被用在神职人员身上，因此同一个形容词也指照料一群「羊」。

senses.title: A bishop's letter to the faithful
senses.definition: a formal letter from a bishop or church leader to the people of a diocese
senses.definitionCN: 主教或教会领袖写给教区信众的正式书信
senses.example: The pastoral letter asked parishes to shelter refugees.
senses.exampleCN: 这封牧函要求各堂区收容难民。
senses.why: a letter that shepherds the readers borrows the adjective of shepherding.
senses.whyCN: 一封「牧养」读者的信，借用了牧养的形容词。

senses.title: A grazing lease in Australian usage
senses.titleCN: 澳大利亚用法中的牧区租地
senses.definition: in Australia, land leased from the state for grazing livestock
senses.definitionCN: 澳大利亚指从国家租来放牧牲畜的土地
senses.example: The family held a pastoral lease of forty thousand hectares.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人持有一份四万公顷的牧区租地。
senses.why: Australian land law named vast dry grazing blocks pastoral, and the adjective became a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 澳大利亚土地法把大片干旱牧地称作 pastoral，形容词于是成了法律类别。

senses.title: Herding that moves with the seasons
senses.definition: describing a herding system that moves animals between seasonal pastures
senses.definitionCN: 形容在季节草场之间移动牲畜的畜牧制度
senses.example: Pastoral nomadism survives where fields cannot be irrigated.
senses.exampleCN: 在无法灌溉的地方，畜牧游牧仍然存续。
senses.why: the adjective combines with nomadism to name the oldest form of livestock keeping.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词与 nomadism 组合，用来命名最古老的养畜形式。

senses.title: A poem about shepherd life
senses.definition: a poem or musical piece in the shepherd convention
senses.definitionCN: 采用牧人套路的诗或乐曲
senses.example: He wrote three pastorals before he ever saw a sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没见过一只羊，就写了三首牧歌。
senses.why: the adjective became a noun for the work itself, a common shift in the language of genres.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成指作品本身的名词，这在体裁语汇里很常见。

intro.en: Pastoral comes from Latin pastoralis, from pastor 'shepherd', built on pascere 'to feed, graze'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pastoral 出自拉丁 pastoralis，再上为 pastor「牧人」，建于 pascere「喂养、放牧」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pascere meant 'to feed, graze'. Its deeper origin is not fully established; the usual link to a root meaning 'to feed' is reconstructed.
items.cn: pascere 意为「喂养、放牧」。其更深来源未有定论；通常与意为「喂养」的词根相联系，那属重构。

items.en: Pastor meant 'herdsman, shepherd', literally 'one who feeds'.
items.cn: pastor 意为「牧人、牧羊人」，字面是「喂养者」。

items.en: Pastoralis meant 'of a shepherd or of shepherding', used of songs, gifts and duties connected with herds.
items.cn: pastoralis 意为「牧人的、牧养的」，用于与牲畜相关的歌、礼物与职责。

items.en: The image of the shepherd was applied to clergy, so pastoral acquired the sense of caring for a congregation.
items.cn: 牧人的意象被用在神职人员身上，pastoral 因此获得「照料会众」的意思。

items.en: English poets of the sixteenth century took pastoral for the shepherd genre, and the idealised countryside followed.
items.cn: 16 世纪英语诗人用 pastoral 指牧歌体裁，理想化的乡野义随之而来。

items.en: Settler land law in Australia named large grazing leases pastoral; the legal sense is dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 澳大利亚移民土地法把大片放牧租地称作 pastoral；这一法律义可定在 19 世纪。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin shepherd and grazing words; the second names the rural and literary qualities pastoral suggests.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁「牧人」「放牧」词；第二组是 pastoral 所暗示的田园与文学品质。

entries.definition: A minister or, literally, a shepherd; the noun for the person where pastoral is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指牧师，字面为牧人；是指人的名词，pastoral 是对应的形容词。

entries.definition: Grassland used for grazing, or to graze it; it names the place or the act, not the style.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于放牧的草地，或放牧这块地；指地点或动作，而非风格。

entries.definition: The branch of farming based on grazing herds; a noun for the economy, not an adjective for a scene.
entries.definitionCN: 指以放牧畜群为基础的农业分支；是经济的名词，不是景象的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who keeps grazing livestock; the human noun, not the literary genre.
entries.definitionCN: 指养放牧牲畜的人；是指人的名词，不是文学体裁。

entries.definition: Charmingly rural in a literary way, from Greek for a herdsman; it is almost always a stylistic word.
entries.definitionCN: 指带文学味的迷人乡野，出自希腊语「牧人」；几乎总是风格用词。

entries.definition: Describing a scene of perfect peace and simplicity; it can apply to any place, not only herding country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容完美宁静朴素的景象；可用于任何地方，不限牧区。

entries.definition: Of the countryside; a neutral word with no idealisation and no herds.
entries.definitionCN: 指乡下的；中性词，不含理想化，也不含畜群。

entries.definition: Relating to land ownership or farming, usually crops; it is about tenure and production, not scenery.
entries.definitionCN: 指与土地所有权或农耕（通常指作物）相关的；讲的是权属与生产，不是风景。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin grazing verb, the family it built and the double life of the word in church and literature.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「放牧」动词、它构成的词族，以及这个词在教会与文学中的双重生活。

normal.en: pascere 'to graze' + -tor 'one who' = pastor, a feeder of animals; pastoral is its adjective.
normal.cn: pascere「放牧」+ -tor「做……的人」= pastor，喂养牲畜的人；pastoral 是其形容词。

normal.en: The family runs pastor, pasture, pastoral, pastoralism and pastoralist.
normal.cn: 词族包括 pastor、pasture、pastoral、pastoralism、pastoralist。

normal.en: The church sense keeps the sheep metaphor: pastoral care, pastoral letter, pastoral visit.
normal.cn: 教会义保留羊的比喻：牧灵关怀、牧函、牧灵探访。

normal.en: The literary sense keeps the golden weather: pastoral poetry, pastoral scene, pastoral elegy.
normal.cn: 文学义保留金色天气：田园诗、田园场景、田园挽歌。

normal.en: In Australia a pastoral lease is a legal category of grazing land.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚，「牧区租约」是放牧土地的一个法律类别。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall that exists only to keep sheep in and the city out.
abstract.cn: 想象一道石墙，唯一的作用是把羊拦住、把城市挡在外面。

abstract.en: Picture a shepherd's crook that is also a bishop's staff.
abstract.cn: 想象一根牧羊杖，同时也是主教的手杖。

abstract.en: Picture a poem written about a field the poet has never walked.
abstract.cn: 想象一首诗写的是诗人从未走过的田野。

examples.en: The region shifted from pastoral use to irrigated horticulture.
examples.cn: 该地区从畜牧用地转为灌溉园艺。

examples.en: Pastoral novels rarely mention the smell of a wet fleece.
examples.cn: 田园小说很少提到湿羊毛的气味。

examples.en: The bishop's pastoral letter was read from every pulpit.
examples.cn: 主教的牧函在每个讲道坛上被宣读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕斯托罗」听成「怕石多罗」——坡上石头多，羊却偏要在石缝里找草，这就是牧羊的田园。pastor 是牧人，pastoral 是牧人的。

root: 拉丁 pastor「牧人」出自 pascere「喂养、放牧」，加 -alis 成 pastoralis「牧人的」；经法语进入英语。基督教把牧人意象用于神职，文学把它用于牧歌体裁，澳大利亚土地法把它用于牧区租地。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide between the working herd and the imagined countryside, then add church care, a bishop's letter, a grazing lease, seasonal herding and the poem itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分布在「干活的畜群」与「想象中的乡野」两侧，再加教会牧养、主教书信、牧区租地、季节畜牧与诗作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry stone wall holding sheep inside and the city outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道干砌石墙，把羊拦在里面，把城市挡在外面。

branches.en: WORKING HERD: settled pasture and seasonal movement are the two practical forms of the same grazing economy.
branches.cn: 干活的畜群：定居牧场与季节移动，是同一畜牧经济的两种实际形态。

branches.en: THE IMAGINED COUNTRY: the idealised scene, the genre and the poem are one literary construction at three stages.
branches.cn: 想象的乡野：理想景象、体裁与诗作，是同一文学建构的三个阶段。

branches.en: THE FLOCK OF PEOPLE: clergy inherit the shepherd image and care for a congregation instead of sheep.
branches.cn: 人的羊群：神职继承了牧人意象，照料的是会众而非羊。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a bishop writes to shepherd his readers.
branches.cn: 书信：主教写信以牧养他的读者。

branches.en: THE LEASE: colonial land law turns the adjective into a legal category of vast dry grazing blocks.
branches.cn: 租地：殖民地土地法把这个形容词变成大片干旱牧地的法律类别。

intro.en: Pastoral is a Latin noun of the shepherd plus a Latin adjective ending; the same stem also built pasture and pastor.
intro.cn: pastoral 是拉丁「牧人」名词加拉丁形容词词尾；同一词干还构成 pasture 与 pastor。

latinIntro.en: Latin pascere 'to graze' also gives pasture, repast and pabulum, all connected with feeding.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pascere「放牧」还给出 pasture、repast、pabulum，都与喂养有关。

items.example: The stem supplies the feeding image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供整个词族背后的「喂养」意象。

items.example: The word moved from sheep to souls.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从羊群移到了灵魂。

items.example: The ending makes pastoralis 'of the shepherd'.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾构成 pastoralis「牧人的」。
画廊里挂满了田园场景。

items.example: The herd moved to summer pasture.

items.meaning: a herding economy or its advocacy
items.exampleCN: 畜牧经济塑造了该地区的法律。

items.meaning: in a rural or shepherd manner
items.exampleCN: 这座山谷有田园式的安静。

items.example: The word literally meant feeding again.
items.exampleCN: 这个词字面意为「再喂一次」。

derivatives.meaning: the quality of being rural and calm

definition_zh: 专利；专利证书；专利权；取得专利；明显的；受专利保护的
definition_en: an exclusive right granted by the state for an invention, or, as an adjective, lying open and therefore clearly visible
core_image: 一只敞开的木匣：图纸摊在众人眼前，独占的许可只交到发明人手上
scene: 小作坊里，老师傅把新做的齿轮装置画成图纸，报给官府，换回一张盖了印的文书。The old workshop filed drawings of its new gear device and came back with a patent.
sceneCN: 这里 patent 是「专利证书」（第 2 个义项：载明独占权的官方文书）；句意：老作坊把新齿轮装置的图纸报了上去，换回一张专利证书。

pos.zh: 明显的；专利的；受专利保护的

derivatives.zh: 由 patent 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地；公然地」
由 patent 加 -ee 构成，义为「专利权人」
由 patent 加 -able 构成，义为「可取得专利的」
由 patentable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可专利性」

senses.title: An exclusive right in an invention
senses.definition: a right given by the state that lets an inventor stop others from making or selling the invention for a set term
senses.definitionCN: 国家授予发明人的权利，可在一定期限内阻止他人制造或销售该发明
senses.example: The lab holds a patent on the cooling method.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室拥有那项冷却方法的专利。
senses.why: Letters patent were open documents by which a ruler granted a privilege, and the invention right inherited that grant.
senses.whyCN: letters patent 是君主授予特权的公开文书，发明权继承了这种「授予」的结构。

senses.title: The document itself
senses.definition: the published document that describes the invention and states the right
senses.definitionCN: 公开描述发明并载明权利的文书
senses.example: The engineer read every page of the patent before designing around it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师逐页读完那份专利，再设法绕开它。
senses.why: The grant was a written instrument, so the paper and the right ended up sharing one name.
senses.whyCN: 授予行为落实为书面文书，于是文书与权利共用一个名称。

senses.title: The protected invention
senses.titleCN: 专利技术；受保护的发明
senses.definition: the technical solution that the document protects, seen as a piece of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 受文书保护的技术方案，被当作一项知识成果
senses.example: The new patent covers a cheaper way to coat glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新专利涵盖一种更便宜的玻璃镀膜方法。
senses.why: Buyers and rivals say the patent when they mean the technology inside it.
senses.whyCN: 买家与对手说「那项专利」时，指的其实是里面的技术。

senses.title: To obtain a patent
senses.definition: to secure a patent for an invention by filing and prosecuting an application
senses.definitionCN: 通过提交并推进申请，为一项发明取得专利
senses.example: They patented the hinge before any rival thought of it.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何对手想到之前，他们就把那个铰链申请了专利。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb as firms began to treat the grant as an action they perform.
senses.whyCN: 当企业开始把「获得授权」当作自己执行的动作，名词就转为动词。

senses.title: Openly evident
senses.definition: so clear that it needs no proof, as in a patent error or a patent lie
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到无需证明，如明显的错误或明显的谎言
senses.example: It was a patent absurdity to insure a ship already sunk.
senses.exampleCN: 给一艘已经沉没的船投保，是明显的荒谬。
senses.why: Patere means to lie open, and what lies open to every eye needs no argument.
senses.whyCN: patere 意为敞开着，对所有人敞开的东西不需要论证。

senses.title: Of or protected by a patent
senses.definition: used before a noun for things belonging to patent law or covered by a patent
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指属于专利法或受某项专利覆盖的
senses.example: Patent rules decide who may sell the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 专利规则决定谁可以销售这种药。
senses.why: As patents became a legal field, the word took on attributive duty and named whatever the field touches.
senses.whyCN: 专利成为法律领域后，这个词承担定语职责，指该领域涉及的一切。

senses.title: A proprietary medicine
senses.definition: a medicine sold under a maker name, historically under letters patent or a proprietary claim
senses.definitionCN: 以厂商名义出售的药品，历史上凭公开特许或专有主张销售
senses.example: Patent medicines were sold by travelling shows a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 一个世纪前，成药由巡回推销的班子售卖。
senses.why: Early remedies carried royal letters patent, and the phrase patent medicine outlived the grant itself.
senses.whyCN: 早期药品带着王室特许状，patent medicine 这个说法比特许制度活得更久。

intro.en: Patent comes from Latin patere, to lie open, through the phrase litterae patentes, open letters that a ruler sent to be read by all.
intro.cn: patent 来自拉丁语 patere（敞开着），经 litterae patentes（供所有人阅读的公开文书）进入英语。

items.en: Patere means to lie open or to be exposed to view.
items.cn: patere 意为敞开着、显露在外。

items.en: Patens, its present participle, means open or uncovered.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 patens 意为敞开的、未遮盖的。

items.en: Litterae patentes are open letters, sealed yet readable by anyone.
items.cn: litterae patentes 是公开文书，盖了印却人人可读。

items.en: Patent carries the sense of open or evident into French.
items.cn: patent 带着「公开、明显」的含义进入法语。

items.en: Patent enters English meaning open or publicly visible.
items.cn: patent 进入英语时意为公开的、众目可见的。

items.en: The open grant of a privilege becomes the patent on an invention.
items.cn: 公开授予的特权演变为针对一项发明的专利权。

note.en: Patent belongs to a family of open and granted words, and it shares its field with copyright, trademark, and licence.
note.cn: patent 属于「公开」与「授予」的词族，并与 copyright、trademark、licence 同处一个法律义场。

entries.definition: in a way that is plainly clear
entries.definitionCN: 明显地；公然地

entries.definition: the person who owns a patent
entries.definitionCN: 专利权人

entries.definition: able to be protected by a patent
entries.definitionCN: 可取得专利的

entries.definition: the right over the copying of a work of authorship
entries.definitionCN: 著作权；版权，与专利权同属知识产权

entries.definition: the registered sign that identifies goods
entries.definitionCN: 商标，与专利并列的另一类工业产权

entries.definition: permission given to use a protected right
entries.definitionCN: 许可；许可证，常与专利许可搭配

normalIntro.en: Patent carries one image through all its senses: something laid open, either a public document or a fact anyone can see.
normalIntro.cn: patent 的各个义项共用一个意象：被摊开的东西，或是一份公开文书，或是一个人尽可见的事实。

normal.en: Patere is Latin for lying open, which is why letters patent were read aloud.
normal.cn: patere 在拉丁语里是「敞开着」，所以公开文书要当众宣读。

normal.en: A patent trades disclosure for a limited monopoly.
normal.cn: 专利用公开技术换一段有限期的独占。

normal.en: Apply for a patent and the office publishes the drawings.
normal.cn: apply for a patent 之后，专利局会把图纸公开。

normal.en: Patent infringement is making the protected invention without permission.
normal.cn: patent infringement 就是未经许可实施受保护的发明。

normal.en: Patently obvious means the same as plainly obvious.
normal.cn: patently obvious 与 plainly obvious 同义，都是「明摆着」。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler opening a chest in public and handing one inventor the key.
abstract.cn: 想象君主当众打开一只匣子，把钥匙只交给一位发明人。

abstract.en: Picture a registry page pinned open so any passer-by can read the drawing.
abstract.cn: 想象登记簿的一页被摊开钉住，路过的人都能读到图纸。

abstract.en: Picture a fence drawn around a blueprint, with a date written on the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象在图纸四周拉起围栏，门口写着一个到期日。

examples.en: The company filed a patent for the new battery in three countries.
examples.cn: 这家公司为新型电池在三个国家申请了专利。

examples.en: The drug is still under patent, so cheap copies cannot be sold.
examples.cn: 这种药仍在专利保护期内，所以不能销售廉价的仿制品。

examples.en: His excuse was a patent lie that nobody in the room believed.
examples.cn: 他的借口是明显的谎言，屋里没人相信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「怕疼」——发明人怕技术被抄得心疼，赶紧去申请专利；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 patere（敞开着）→ 现在分词 patens（公开的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 litterae patentes（公开文书）→ 英语 patent，核心义是「公开授予的独占权」，形容词义「明显的」直接来自「敞开着」。

sensesIntro.en: Patent begins with the open grant and its paper, moves to the protected technology and the act of obtaining it, then splits into the adjective of open evidence and the narrow field uses.
sensesIntro.cn: patent 先指公开的授予行为与那份文书，再指受保护的技术与取得专利的动作，随后分出「明显」的形容词义与几个领域用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document laid open on a table, with one inventor holding a sealed permit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份摊在桌上的文书，只有一位发明人握着盖印的许可。

branches.en: The granted right is the legal centre of the word.
branches.cn: 被授予的权利是这个词的法律中心。

branches.en: The paper that records the grant is the documentary sense.
branches.cn: 记录授予的纸质文书是文献义项。

branches.en: The technology inside the paper is what engineers mean by the patent.
branches.cn: 文书里的技术，是工程师说「那项专利」时的所指。

branches.en: The verb of obtaining and the attributive field use both grow from the grant.
branches.cn: 取得专利的动词义与领域定语用法，都从「授予」长出来。

branches.en: Open evidence and the old proprietary medicine keep the original open sense.
branches.cn: 「明显」的公开证据义与旧的成药义，都保留了最初的「敞开」义。

intro.en: Patent is built on the Latin verb patere and its participle, then grows English branches through -ee, -able, and -ly.
intro.cn: patent 建立在拉丁语动词 patere 及其分词之上，再借 -ee、-able、-ly 长出英语的分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin patere means to lie open; patens means open, and litterae patentes means open letters.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 patere 意为敞开；patens 意为敞开的；litterae patentes 意为公开文书。

items.meaning: to lie open, to be exposed
items.example: Patere supplies the open image behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: patere 提供所有义项背后的「敞开」意象。

items.example: Patens is the participle that carries the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: patens 是承载形容词义的分词。

items.example: The phrase names the document a ruler sent to be read by all.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语指君主发出、供所有人阅读的文书。

items.example: Patent keeps the grant sense in law.
items.exampleCN: patent 在法律中保留「授予」义。

items.example: The verb names what inventors do.
items.exampleCN: 动词义指发明人所做的事。

items.example: Letters patent keeps the medieval phrase in modern law.
items.exampleCN: letters patent 把中世纪的说法留在现代法律里。

definition_zh: 病原体；病原微生物（引起疾病的生物）
definition_en: a bacterium, virus, fungus or other organism that causes disease in a host
core_image: 一个微生物钻进宿主组织，宿主的细胞开始受损
scene: 这里指「病原体」。 A pathogen can enter the body through a cut in the skin.
sceneCN: 这里 pathogen 指「病原体」（第 1 个义项：能引起疾病的微生物或其他生物）；句意：病原体可以通过皮肤上的伤口进入身体。图中可辨识物件：皮肤破口、微生物、宿主细胞、侵入箭头。

pos.zh: 病原体；病原微生物（细菌、病毒、真菌、朊病毒等引起疾病者）

derivatives.zh: 致病的；病原的
致病性
病理学；病变
发病机制
病原基因组学

senses.title: Disease-causing microbe
senses.titleCN: 病原体：引起疾病的微生物
senses.definition: a microorganism, such as a bacterium or a virus, that causes disease when it enters or colonises a host
senses.definitionCN: 进入或定植宿主后引起疾病的微生物，如细菌或病毒
senses.example: A pathogen can enter the body through a cut in the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 病原体可以通过皮肤上的伤口进入身体。
senses.why: Greek pathos 'suffering' plus -gen 'producing' names the germ by its result: the thing that produces suffering.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 pathos「痛苦」加 -gen「产生」按结果给微生物命名：制造痛苦的东西。

senses.title: Any biological agent
senses.titleCN: 广义病原：病毒、真菌、朊病毒等一切致病生物因子
senses.definition: any biological agent that causes disease, including viruses, fungi, protozoa, helminths and prions, not only bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 任何引起疾病的生物因子，包括病毒、真菌、原虫、蠕虫与朊病毒，而不只是细菌
senses.example: Fungi and prions are pathogens too, although neither is a bacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌与朊病毒也是病原体，尽管两者都不是细菌。
senses.why: The word names a role rather than a taxonomic class, so anything that reliably causes disease in a host can fill that role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一个角色而非分类类群，因此任何能稳定引起宿主疾病的东西都能承担这一角色。

senses.title: Opportunistic pathogen
senses.titleCN: 机会性病原：通常不致病的条件致病微生物
senses.definition: a germ that normally causes no harm but becomes pathogenic when the host's defences are weakened
senses.definitionCN: 通常不造成伤害、但在宿主防御减弱时转为致病的微生物
senses.example: The fungus is an opportunistic pathogen in patients with low immunity.
senses.exampleCN: 这种真菌在免疫力低下的患者中是机会性病原。
senses.why: Pathogenicity depends on the host as much as the germ, so a harmless resident can be reclassified when the body's guard drops.
senses.whyCN: 致病性既取决于病原也取决于宿主，因此无害的常驻菌在身体防线下降时可被重新归类。

senses.title: Plant pathogen
senses.titleCN: 植物病原体：引起作物病害的生物
senses.definition: an organism that causes disease in plants, such as a fungus, bacterium or virus affecting crops
senses.definitionCN: 引起植物疾病的生物，如影响作物的真菌、细菌或病毒
senses.example: A soil-borne pathogen wiped out half the wheat field.
senses.exampleCN: 一种土传病原毁掉了半片麦田。
senses.why: Agriculture faces the same triangle of host, germ and environment, so the medical word was applied to crops without change.
senses.whyCN: 农业面对同样的宿主、病原与环境三角，因此医学用词原封不动地用到了作物上。

senses.title: Foodborne pathogen
senses.titleCN: 食源性病原：随食物进入人体的致病微生物
senses.definition: a germ carried by food or water that causes illness after being swallowed
senses.definitionCN: 由食物或水携带、被吞下后引起疾病的微生物
senses.example: Inspectors test for foodborne pathogens such as Salmonella.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员检测沙门氏菌等食源性病原。
senses.why: The route of entry defines a public health category, so the general word is used with a modifier for the food route.
senses.whyCN: 进入途径界定了公共卫生类别，因此这个总称与修饰语连用，指经食物进入的那一类。

senses.title: Biothreat agent
senses.titleCN: 生物威胁病原：被管控的高危病原
senses.definition: a pathogen dangerous enough to be regulated, listed or secured as a biological threat
senses.definitionCN: 危险到需要被管控、列入名录或加以保安的病原体
senses.example: The laboratory is licensed to work with select-agent pathogens.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验室获准研究特定管制病原。
senses.why: Security and law needed a neutral word that covers germs and toxins without promising that they are weapons, and pathogen supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 安全与法律需要一个中性词来涵盖病原与毒素，又不直接宣称它们是武器，pathogen 正好补上。

senses.title: Pathogen load
senses.titleCN: 病原负荷：体内病原的数量或密度
senses.definition: the amount or density of a pathogen present in a host, tissues or an environment
senses.definitionCN: 宿主、组织或环境中存在的病原数量或密度
senses.example: High pathogen load predicts a worse outcome in sepsis.
senses.exampleCN: 病原负荷高预示脓毒症的预后更差。
senses.why: Disease severity often tracks how much germ is present, so 'load' turns the countable organism into a measurable burden.
senses.whyCN: 病情严重程度常随病原量变化，因此「负荷」这一说法把可数的微生物变成一个可测量的负担。

senses.title: Emerging pathogen
senses.titleCN: 新发病原：新出现或重新流行的病原
senses.definition: a pathogen that has recently appeared in a population, changed its host range or rapidly increased its spread
senses.definitionCN: 近期在人群中出现的病原，或已改变宿主范围、迅速扩大传播的病原
senses.example: Surveillance exists to catch an emerging pathogen early.
senses.exampleCN: 监测系统的存在就是为了及早发现新发病原。
senses.why: The word is a role, and roles can be newly acquired: a germ harmless in one species can become a pathogen when it crosses into another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是一个角色，而角色可以被新获得：在一个物种中无害的微生物，跨入另一物种后便能成为病原体。

intro.en: Pathogen joins Greek pathos 'suffering, disease' to -gen 'producing'. It is a nineteenth-century scientific coinage, made when specific germs were being linked to specific diseases.
intro.cn: pathogen 把希腊 pathos「痛苦、疾病」接到 -gen「产生」上。它是 19 世纪的科学新造词，诞生于「特定微生物对应特定疾病」的研究时期。

items.en: Pathos meant what is suffered: experience, emotion, and in medical writing disease or suffering. It is the root of pathology, sympathy and pathetic.
items.cn: pathos 指所承受之事：经验、情感，在医学文献中指疾病或痛苦。它是 pathology、sympathy、pathetic 的词根。

items.en: The suffix -genes meant 'born of, produced by'; medical Latin shortened it to -gen, so a pathogen is literally a 'suffering-producer'.
items.cn: 后缀 -genes 意为「由…所生、由…产生」；医学拉丁缩为 -gen，因此 pathogen 字面即「痛苦制造者」。

items.en: In the 1870s and 1880s Koch and Pasteur showed that particular microbes cause particular diseases; researchers then needed a general noun for the causal organism.
items.cn: 1870 至 1880 年代，科赫与巴斯德证明特定微生物引起特定疾病；研究者随后需要一个通称来指致病生物。

items.en: The compound pathogen is recorded in the late nineteenth century, usually dated to the 1880s; it was built on the existing Greek elements rather than inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 复合词 pathogen 记录于 19 世纪后期，通常定在 1880 年代；它用现成的希腊成分构成，并非从拉丁语继承。

items.en: Twentieth-century science extended it beyond bacteria to viruses, fungi, protozoa and prions, and to plant and environmental contexts.
items.cn: 20 世纪科学把它从细菌扩展到病毒、真菌、原虫与朊病毒，并延伸到植物与环境语境。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first date and first author of pathogen are not firmly established; the 1880s attribution is an approximation based on the growth of germ theory.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与首创者存疑）：pathogen 的确切首见年代与首位使用者都无定论；1880 年代之说只是依据病菌学说发展的约数。

note.en: The first group holds words built from the same Greek pieces or differing by one suffix; the second holds biological and clinical terms that are often used where pathogen appears.
note.cn: 第一组是用同样的希腊部件构成、或只差一个后缀的词；第二组是常与 pathogen 同处一句的生物学与临床术语。

entries.definition: Meaning 'disease-causing'; it describes a germ, while pathogen names the germ itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「致病的」；它形容病原，pathogen 则命名病原本身。

entries.definition: The study of disease and its effects on tissues; it shares the pathos root but names a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究疾病及其对组织影响的学科；共享 pathos 词根，但命名的是一门学问。

entries.definition: A substance the immune system recognises; a pathogen carries antigens but an antigen need not be alive.
entries.definitionCN: 免疫系统识别的物质；病原携带抗原，但抗原不必是活物。

entries.definition: A parasite lives at another organism's expense; only some parasites cause disease, and only those are pathogens.
entries.definitionCN: 寄生物以另一生物为代价生存；只有部分寄生物引起疾病，也只有那些才是病原体。

entries.definition: A informal term for a microbe that causes disease; pathogen is the technical equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指标病原微生物的词；pathogen 是技术对应词。

entries.definition: Any microscopic organism; most microbes are harmless, so microbe is broader than pathogen.
entries.definitionCN: 任何微小生物；多数微生物无害，因此 microbe 比 pathogen 宽。

entries.definition: An organism such as a mosquito that carries a pathogen from one host to another.
entries.definitionCN: 把病原从一个宿主带到另一个宿主的生物，如蚊子。

entries.definition: The measure of how much damage a pathogen causes; being a pathogen is the role, virulence is the strength.
entries.definitionCN: 病原造成损害程度的量；作为病原体是一种角色，毒力是强度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: patho- 'disease' + -gen 'producing' = 'disease-producer'.
normal.cn: patho-「疾病」+ -gen「产生」=「疾病制造者」。

normal.en: The family runs pathogen, pathogenic, pathogenicity, pathogenesis, pathology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pathogen、pathogenic、pathogenicity、pathogenesis、pathology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the host: plant pathogen, foodborne pathogen, emerging pathogen.
normal.cn: 固定搭配命名宿主：植物病原、食源性病原、新发病原。

normal.en: A pathogen is defined by the disease it causes, not by its species.
normal.cn: 病原体按它引起的疾病定义，而不是按物种定义。

normal.en: Do not confuse pathogen with antigen: the germ versus the molecule the immune system sees.
normal.cn: 不要把 pathogen 与 antigen 混同：一个是病原，一个是免疫系统所见的分子。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny visitor that is defined entirely by the trouble it leaves behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一位极小的访客，它的身份完全由留下的麻烦来定义。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a door only in a weakened house.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，只在虚弱的房子里才打得开门。

abstract.en: Picture a harmless passenger that changes role when it crosses a border.
abstract.cn: 想象一个无害的乘客，一旦越过边界就换了角色。

examples.en: The pathogen is spread by droplets from the nose and throat.
examples.cn: 该病原通过鼻咽飞沫传播。

examples.en: Researchers sequenced the pathogen to track its origin.
examples.cn: 研究者对病原测序以追踪其来源。

examples.en: Some pathogens survive for days on dry surfaces.
examples.cn: 有些病原能在干燥表面存活数天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「patho 病 + gen 产生」——产生疾病的东西 → pathogen 病原体

root: 希腊 pathos「痛苦；疾病」+ 希腊 -genes「产生」→ 英语 pathogen（19 世纪后期，1880 年代前后）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: the disease-causing microbe, the wider class of biological agents, the germ that waits for weakness, the crop-destroying and food-carried forms, the regulated threat, the measured load, and the germ that has newly acquired the role.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个角色展开：致病的微生物、更宽的生物因子类别、等待宿主虚弱的病原、毁坏作物与随食物进入的类型、被管控的威胁、被计量的负荷，以及新近获得该角色的病原。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a microbe entering a host and leaving damage behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个微生物进入宿主，留下损害。

branches.en: THE ROLE: the basic germ, then the full range of biological agents.
branches.cn: 角色：基本微生物，然后是全部生物因子范围。

branches.en: DEPENDENCE ON THE HOST: a resident becomes a pathogen when defences fail.
branches.cn: 依赖宿主：常驻者只在防线崩溃时成为病原。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES, OTHER ROUTES: crops and food carry the same kind of threat.
branches.cn: 其他身体、其他途径：作物与食物携带同一类威胁。

branches.en: SECURITY: danger becomes a legal category and a select list.
branches.cn: 安全：危险变成法律类别与管制名录。

branches.en: MEASURE AND CHANGE: load counts the burden, emergence marks a new role.
branches.cn: 量与变：负荷计量负担，新发表明角色更新。

intro.en: Pathogen is patho- 'disease' plus -gen 'producing'; the family replaces -gen with -genic, -genicity and -genesis.
intro.cn: pathogen 是 patho-「疾病」加 -gen「产生」；词族把 -gen 换成 -genic、-genicity、-genesis。

latinIntro.en: Both elements are Greek: pathos and -genes. Latin supplies only the scientific ending conventions, not the root, so the compound is Greek throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部件都来自希腊语：pathos 与 -genes。拉丁语只提供科学词尾的书写惯例，不提供词根，因此整词属希腊来源。

items.example: The pathogen was isolated from the blood.
items.exampleCN: 病原从血液中分离出来。

items.example: Many pathogens share the same entry route.
items.exampleCN: 许多病原共享同一进入途径。

items.example: Only a few strains are pathogenic.
items.exampleCN: 只有少数毒株是致病的。

items.example: The pathogenesis begins at the gut wall.

items.exampleCN: 病理学证实了组织损伤。

items.meaningCN: 应用于病原的基因组学
items.exampleCN: 病原基因组学追踪新变异。
该植物病原通过土壤传播。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 痛苦；疾病；情感（希腊语，非拉丁语）
出生；产生（希腊语，-genes 的动词来源）

definition_zh: 图案；模式；规律；纸样；范例；（动词）仿照；以图案装饰
definition_en: a repeated design or a regular arrangement; a model to copy; also a verb meaning to model something on another or to decorate with a design
core_image: 一个方块被刻成印版，压到布上，再压一次、又一次，同样的形状排成一片
scene: 裁缝铺的长桌上摊开一张纸样，粉笔线在布面上勾出重复的方格，The tailor pins the paper pattern onto the cloth before cutting.
sceneCN: 这里 pattern 指「裁剪用的纸样模板」（第 3 个义项：供复制用的样板）；句意为裁缝把纸质样板别到布上再下剪。图中可辨识物件：长桌、纸样、粉笔线、别针与格纹布面；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 有图案的；按模式排列的
图案形成；模式化

senses.title: A repeated decorative design
senses.definition: a design of repeated shapes, lines or colours used to decorate a surface
senses.definitionCN: 由重复的形状、线条或色彩构成、用于装饰表面的图样
senses.example: The curtains carry a small floral pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘上带着细小的花卉图案。
senses.why: The word began as patron, 'a model to copy'; decoration repeats a copied unit across a surface.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初借自意为「可复制的范本」的外来词；装饰正是把一个被复制的单元铺满表面。

senses.title: A recurring sequence of events
senses.definition: a regular and repeated way in which events or actions occur
senses.definitionCN: 事件或行为有规律地反复出现的方式
senses.example: The patient's sleep pattern changed after the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行之后，这位患者的睡眠规律变了。
senses.why: Once a model is repeated in time rather than on a surface, the repetition itself becomes the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当范本不是铺在表面、而是在时间中反复，重复本身就成了模式。

senses.title: A template or model for making copies
senses.titleCN: 供复制使用的样板或模板
senses.definition: a shape or model used as a guide for cutting, sewing or casting
senses.definitionCN: 裁剪、缝制或浇铸时用作依据的形状或模型
senses.example: She pinned the paper pattern to the fabric and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 她把纸质样板别到布上，沿粉笔线剪开。
senses.why: This is the literal ancestor: a pattern is first an object you lay down and copy.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的祖先义：pattern 最初就是一件可以铺下来照着复制的东西。

senses.title: The arrangement of parts that forms a whole
senses.definition: the way elements are arranged or organized in a whole
senses.definitionCN: 各要素在整体中被排列或组织的方式
senses.example: The novel's pattern of images returns in the last chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 小说中那组意象的排列在最后一章再次出现。
senses.why: From a copied outline the sense broadens to any arrangement whose parts answer one another.
senses.whyCN: 从可复制的轮廓出发，词义扩展到任何部件彼此呼应的排列。

senses.title: A regularity detected in data or nature
senses.titleCN: 在数据或自然中找出的规律
senses.definition: a recognizable regularity in measurements, behaviour or natural forms
senses.definitionCN: 在测量、行为或自然形态中可辨认的规律性
senses.example: The software looks for patterns in the sales figures.
senses.exampleCN: 软件在销售数据中寻找规律。
senses.why: Science makes the repetition an object of search: the pattern is the order found in what looked random.
senses.whyCN: 科学把重复变成搜寻的对象：模式就是从看似随机之物里找出的秩序。

senses.title: A recurring arrangement in language
senses.titleCN: 语言中反复出现的结构
senses.definition: a regular arrangement of sounds or words that speakers of a language follow
senses.definitionCN: 说某种语言的人所遵循的、语音或词句的规律性排列
senses.example: The drill fixes the sentence pattern in memory.
senses.exampleCN: 反复操练把句型固定在记忆里。
senses.why: Language is learned through repeated shapes, so the same word names the frames a speaker reuses.
senses.whyCN: 语言通过反复的形状被学会，同一个词便用来命名说话者反复套用的框架。

senses.title: A model of conduct held up for imitation
senses.definition: an example or model of behaviour that others are expected to follow
senses.definitionCN: 他人应当效仿的行为榜样或范例
senses.example: The older teachers were held up as a pattern of patience.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年长的教师被举为耐心的典范。
senses.why: This restores the Latin model sense: patronus was a protector and an exemplar, and pattern kept that moral use into modern English.
senses.whyCN: 这恢复了拉丁语的范本义：patronus 既是保护人也是榜样，pattern 把这一道德用法保留到现代英语。

senses.title: To model something on, or decorate with a design
senses.definition: to make or shape something according to a model, or to decorate a surface with a regular design
senses.definitionCN: 依照某个范本制作或塑造某物，或以规则图样装饰表面
senses.example: The garden was patterned on a larger estate in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园是仿照北方一处更大的庄园建造的。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: whatever follows a model is patterned on it, and a surface given a repeated design is patterned too.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：照着范本做的，就是依范本而制；被赋予重复图样的表面也可说带图样的。

intro.en: Pattern comes from Middle English patron, taken from Latin patronus 'protector, model', which was built on pater 'father'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pattern 来自中古英语的借形，后者出自拉丁语 patronus「保护人、范本」，而 patronus 由 pater「父亲」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pater meant 'father'. It is the base of patronus and also of English words about fatherhood and protection.
items.cn: pater 意为「父亲」。它既是 patronus 的词基，也是一批表示父系与保护的英语词的来源。

items.en: The suffix -onus built nouns of role or function; added to pater it produced patronus, 'one who acts as a father to others'.
items.cn: 后缀 -onus 构成表示角色或职能的名词；加在 pater 上便产生 patronus，意为「替他人承担父职的人」。

items.en: Patronus meant 'protector, defender' and, in later Latin, 'a model or example to be followed'.
items.cn: patronus 意为「保护人、辩护者」，在后期拉丁语中又指「可供效法的范本或榜样」。

items.en: English took patron through Old French, where it kept both the protector and the model senses.
items.cn: 英语经由古法语接受这个借形，古法语同时保留了保护人与范本两种含义。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling shifted from patron to pattern, and the 'model' sense moved to the centre of the word.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，拼写最终定为 pattern，「范本」义逐渐成为这个词的核心。

items.en: Source uncertain: why the written form settled as pattern rather than patron is not fully explained; sixteenth-century spelling habits are generally assumed to be the cause.
items.cn: 来源不确定：书写形式为何最终定为 pattern 而非较早的借形，尚无完满解释；一般认为与 16 世纪的拼写习惯有关。

note.en: The first group holds words that look close to pattern, including its own ancestor; the second holds words for design and for models to copy, which differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 pattern 的词，其中包含它自己的祖先形式；第二组指图案与可复制的范本，各自强调的方面不同。

entries.definition: A person who supports or protects someone; this is the form English borrowed first, before pattern took over the model sense.
entries.definitionCN: 支持或保护他人的人；这是英语最先借入的形式，后来 pattern 才承担了范本义。

entries.definition: An official right to an invention; from Latin patere 'to lie open', with no link to pater 'father'.
entries.definitionCN: 对发明享有的官方专有权；来自拉丁语 patere「敞开」，与 pater「父亲」无关。

entries.definition: A wooden shoe or clog worn to raise the foot above mud; it only sounds like pattern and has no shared sense with it.
entries.definitionCN: 垫高脚步以免陷入泥中的木鞋或木套鞋；只是读音像 pattern，意义并无交集。

entries.definition: The planned arrangement of lines, shapes or colours; design can be invented rather than repeated, while pattern stresses repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 对线条、形状或色彩的规划性安排；设计可以原创而不必重复，pattern 则强调重复。

entries.definition: One repeated figure within a design; a motif is the unit that a pattern repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 图案中反复出现的单个图形；母题正是被图案重复的那个单元。

entries.definition: A shaped guide for cutting or drawing; it is the physical model sense of pattern, without the decorative senses.
entries.definitionCN: 裁剪或描画用的成形样板；它就是 pattern 的实体范本义，不含装饰性的义项。

entries.definition: A thing or person taken as an example to copy; model is wider and also covers scale models and abstract systems.
entries.definitionCN: 被拿来照着做的物或人；model 范围更广，还包括缩比模型与抽象系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Pattern began as patron, a model to copy.
normal.cn: pattern 最初借自一个意为「可照抄的范本」的外来词。

normal.en: A pattern repeats one unit across a surface, like a stamp pressed again and again.
normal.cn: 图案是把一个单元铺满表面，像印章一次次压下去。

normal.en: The paper pattern in a sewing shop is a model laid on cloth.
normal.cn: 裁缝铺里的纸质样板，就是铺在布上的模型。

normal.en: Weather patterns repeat in time, not on a wall.
normal.cn: 天气模式在时间中重复，而不是在墙上重复。

normal.en: Pattern recognition is the search for order in what first looks random.
normal.cn: 模式识别就是在初看杂乱之处寻找秩序。

abstract.en: Picture a single tile copied until the whole floor becomes a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一块瓷砖被不断复制，直到整个地面成为一个故事。

abstract.en: Picture a river that cuts the same bend every year.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河每年都切出同一个弯。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence frame that many different words can step into.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子框架，许多不同的词都能走进去。

examples.en: The tiles form a geometric pattern across the floor.
examples.cn: 瓷砖在地面上构成几何图案。

examples.en: Doctors noticed a pattern in the patients' symptoms.
examples.cn: 医生们注意到患者的症状中有一种规律。

examples.en: The new school was patterned on a design from the coast.
examples.cn: 这所新学校是仿照沿海地区的一个设计建造的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派藤」——藤条编出的格子一遍遍重复，派上去铺满就成图案。patron 本是「范本」，照着范本一次次复制，就有了 pattern。

root: 中古英语的借形来自拉丁语 patronus「保护人、范本」；patronus 由 pater「父亲」加名词后缀 -onus 构成。拼写后来变为 pattern，「范本、样板」义成为核心，再引申出图案、模式与规律等义。拼写变化的具体原因属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a repeated decorative design, then move to a sequence in time and a model cut from paper, to arrangement and detected regularity, to language and moral example, and end with the verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从重复的装饰图案开始，转到时间中的次序与纸质样板，再到部件排列与被找出的规律，再到语言结构与道德典范，最后是动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one unit is stamped, cut or copied again and again, so repetition itself becomes the visible order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个单元被反复压印、裁剪或复制，重复本身成了可见的秩序。

branches.en: THE REPEATED UNIT: the core sense is a copied shape repeated across a surface until the surface is covered.
branches.cn: 重复的单元：核心义是一个被复制的形状在表面上反复出现，直到铺满。

branches.en: REPETITION IN TIME OR ON PAPER: a habit repeats on a schedule, and a template is the model laid down before the copy is made.
branches.cn: 在时间中或在纸上的重复：习惯按时间表反复，样板则是复制之前铺下的模型。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND ORDER: the word widens from a visible design to the way parts fit a whole, and then to a regularity found in data.
branches.cn: 排列与秩序：词义从可见图样扩展到部件构成整体的方式，再扩展到数据中被找出的规律。

branches.en: A SHAPE OTHERS COPY: a sentence frame is reused by speakers, and a moral example is held up for others to follow.
branches.cn: 被别人复制的形状：句型被说话者反复套用，道德榜样则被举出来供人效法。

branches.en: THE ACTION OF COPYING: the noun becomes a verb, so a thing can be patterned on a model or patterned with a design.
branches.cn: 复制的动作：名词转为动词，于是可以说某物仿照某个范本，或表面被赋予图样。

intro.en: Pattern can be read as a Latin noun base, a Latin role suffix and the English word that grew out of them, plus two adjective endings.
intro.cn: pattern 可以读作一个拉丁名词词基、一个拉丁角色后缀、由它们生长出来的英语词，再加两个形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pater 'father' with -onus produced patronus 'protector, model'; English shortened it to patron, respelled it pattern, and later added -ed and -less.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pater「父亲」加 -onus 构成 patronus「保护人、范本」；英语先缩略这个词形，再改写为 pattern，后来又加两个词尾构成形容词。

items.example: The noun supplies the family image behind the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供拉丁词背后的家族意象。

items.meaning: one who acts in a role or function
items.meaningCN: 承担某种角色或职能的人
items.example: The suffix turns 'father' into a word for one who protects others.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「父亲」变成表示保护他人者之词。

items.example: Latin used the noun for a protector and later for an example.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指保护人，后来也指榜样。

items.example: English kept the older form beside its respelled doublet.
items.exampleCN: 英语把较旧的形式与改写后的同源词并存在一起。

items.structure: pattern (English noun and verb, respelled from patron)
items.meaning: a repeated design; a model to copy
items.meaningCN: 重复的图案；可复制的范本
items.example: The respelled form took over the model and design senses.
items.exampleCN: 改写后的形式承接了范本与图案两种含义。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective of possession.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示拥有的形容词。

items.meaning: having a pattern; modelled on something
items.example: The fabric is patterned with small squares.
items.exampleCN: 这块布上有小方格图案。

items.example: The suffix removes the quality the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀去掉名词所指的性质。

derivatives.meaning: the noun of design shifts to an adjective meaning 'provided with a pattern' or 'modelled on something'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由表示图案的名词转为形容词，表示「带有图案」或「仿照某物」

derivatives.meaning: the noun shifts to an adjective meaning 'having no pattern'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由名词转为形容词，表示「没有图案的」

definition_zh: 付款；款项；报答
definition_en: the act of paying money, a sum of money that is paid, or something given in return for what someone has done
core_image: 一只信封从一只手递到另一只手里，封口处写着金额
scene: 月底的办公室里，会计把一叠单据摊在桌上。The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里是「付款、支付」（第 1 个义项：付钱这一行为）；句意为公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。图中可辨识物件：单据、计算器、贴着标签的信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 payment 去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的基础动词，义为「支付」
由 pay 加 -able 构成，指应付的、可支付的
由 pay 加 -er 构成，指付款的一方
由 pay 加 -ee 构成，指收款的一方

senses.title: The act of paying money
senses.definition: the act of giving money for goods, work or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为货物、劳动或服务把钱交出去这一行为
senses.example: The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns a verb into the name of its action, so payment names the handing over itself rather than the money.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成动作的名称，所以 payment 先指「把钱交出去」这件事，而不是那笔钱。

senses.title: An amount of money paid
senses.definition: a sum of money that is paid or that has to be paid
senses.definitionCN: 已经付出或按约定需要付出的一笔钱
senses.example: The first payment is due at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 第一期款项在月底到期。
senses.why: Once the action has a name, the thing produced by the action takes the same noun, which is why payments can be counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 动作有了名称之后，动作产生的东西也用同一个名词，所以一笔一笔的款项可以数出来。

senses.title: A return for what someone has done
senses.definition: something given or suffered as a return for what a person has done
senses.definitionCN: 因某人做过的事而得到或承受的回报
senses.example: That was payment for years of neglect.
senses.exampleCN: 那是对多年冷落的报应。
senses.why: If paying is giving back what is owed, then any return can be called payment, and the word stretches from wages to punishment.
senses.whyCN: 既然付款是归还所欠，那么任何回报都可以叫 payment，这个词便从报酬一路延伸到惩罚。

intro.en: Payment is the English noun built on pay, and both go back through French to a Latin word for peace.
intro.cn: payment 是在 pay 之上构成的英语名词，二者都经法语回溯到一个表示和平的拉丁词。

items.en: Pax meant peace, and settling a claim was understood as restoring quiet between two sides.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，结清一笔索求被理解为让双方之间恢复安静。

items.en: The verb pacare meant to quiet or satisfy someone, and in medieval use it covered satisfying a creditor with money.
items.cn: 动词 pacare 意为使某人平静或满足，在中世纪的用法里包括用钱让债主满足。

items.en: Old French formed paiement from payer, adding its own noun ending to the verb for paying.
items.cn: 古法语由 payer 造出 paiement，给表示支付的动词加上自己的名词词尾。

items.en: Anglo-French carried the word into English legal and commercial writing, where fixed sums and dates mattered.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语把这个词带进英语的法律与商业文书，那里讲究固定的金额与日期。

items.en: Modern English keeps payment for the act, for each sum, and for a return of any kind, while pay names the wages themselves.
items.cn: 现代英语用 payment 指行为、每一笔金额以及任何形式的回报，而 pay 指工钱本身。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base verb, the two person forms and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for sums paid and for closing an account.
note.cn: 形近组收基础动词、两个指人的形式，以及一个只是外形相似的词；近义组收表示所付金额与结清账目的词。

entries.definition: The verb that payment is built on, meaning to give money for something.
entries.definitionCN: payment 所依附的动词，意为为某物付钱。

entries.definition: That must be paid, or able to be paid.
entries.definitionCN: 应付的，或可支付的。

entries.definition: The person who receives a payment.
entries.definitionCN: 收到款项的人。

entries.definition: The hard surface beside a road, from a Latin verb meaning to beat down; only the ending looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 路旁的硬质路面，来自一个意为「夯平」的拉丁动词；只是词尾相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Money paid for a service or for a right.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项服务或某项权利付出的钱。

entries.definition: One of several fixed sums paid over a period.
entries.definitionCN: 分几期付出的一笔固定金额。

entries.definition: Money sent to someone, especially by post or transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 汇给某人的钱，尤指通过邮寄或转账。

entries.definition: The act of paying what is owed and ending a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 付清欠款并了结索求的行为。

normalIntro.en: The word is a verb plus a noun ending, and behind the verb sits a Latin idea of peace; the whole family is about making a claim go quiet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是动词加名词词尾，动词背后是拉丁语中「和平」的观念；整族词都在说让一项索求安静下来。

normal.en: Payment is pay plus -ment, the ending that turns an action into a noun, as in movement and argument.
normal.cn: payment 是 pay 加 -ment，这个后缀把动作变成名词，就像 movement 与 argument。

normal.en: Old French had paiement, so English did not invent the noun; it borrowed a ready-made form.
normal.cn: 古法语已有 paiement，英语并没有自造这个名词，而是借了一个现成的形式。

normal.en: Make a payment is the everyday phrase, because the noun names the act rather than a thing you can hold.
normal.cn: make a payment 是日常说法，因为这个名词指行为，而不是手里能拿住的东西。

normal.en: A down payment is the sum handed over first, before the rest follows in instalments.
normal.cn: down payment 是先交出的那一笔，其余部分随后分期付清。

normal.en: With payment the focus is on the act or the sum; with pay it is on the wages as a whole.
normal.cn: 用 payment 时焦点在行为或某一笔钱；用 pay 时焦点在作为整体的工钱。

abstract.en: Adding -ment to a verb is a way of freezing an action into something a contract can name.
abstract.cn: 给动词加 -ment，是把一个动作冻成合同可以指名的那样东西。

abstract.en: A payment is a promise made visible: the moment an obligation turns into something countable.
abstract.cn: 一笔付款是让承诺变得可见的时刻：义务变成了可以计数的东西。

abstract.en: The word keeps the old idea that money quiets a claim, which is why even a punishment can be called its payment.
abstract.cn: 这个词保留了「钱让索求安静」的旧观念，所以连惩罚也可以被称为它的报应。

examples.en: The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
examples.cn: 公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。

examples.en: The first payment is due at the end of the month.
examples.cn: 第一期款项在月底到期。

examples.en: They accept payment by card or by bank transfer.
examples.cn: 他们接受刷卡或银行转账付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赔门特」——像「赔」加上一道门，钱从门里递出去；payment 就是付出去的款。

root: pay（支付）加名词后缀 -ment 构成；pay 源自拉丁语 pax（和平）与 pacare（使平静、清偿），经古法语 payer 与 paiement 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of handing money over; from that act come the single sum paid and the wider idea of any return, good or bad.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把钱交出去这个动作；由它分出所付的一笔金额，以及任何回报（无论好坏）这一更宽的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed envelope passing from one hand to another, an amount written across the flap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只封好的信封从一只手递到另一只手里，封口上写着金额。

branches.en: a transfer completed before a deadline
branches.cn: 在截止前完成的一笔转账

branches.en: a numbered first sum due at month end
branches.cn: 月底到期、编号为第一期的一笔钱

branches.en: an old neglect finally answered
branches.cn: 多年的冷落终于得到回应

branches.en: the act and the sum share one noun
branches.cn: 行为与金额共用一个名词

branches.en: what is counted and what is returned
branches.cn: 被计数的那笔与被归还的那份

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted verb with an English noun ending, and the Latin root itself began as a word for peace.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根的动词加上英语名词词尾，而那个拉丁词根本身最初表示和平。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 豌豆；豌豆粒；豌豆状的小圆物
definition_en: a round green seed that grows in a long pod and is eaten as a vegetable; also a small round object that looks like this seed
core_image: 拇指沿着豆荚的缝一压，一排圆豆滚进掌心
scene: 菜园里藤蔓顺着竹架往上爬，几个鼓鼓的豆荚垂在叶子下面。He split a pod open and the small green peas rolled across the cutting board.
sceneCN: 这里是「豌豆」（第 1 个义项：长在豆荚里的绿色圆粒）；句意是他掰开一个豆荚，小小的绿豌豆滚到了砧板上。画面里有竹架、豆荚与砧板。

pos.zh: 豌豆；豌豆粒；豌豆状小圆物

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 pisum 经古英语 pise 演变而来的旧式集体名词，后来被复数 peas 取代，义为「豌豆（总称）」
由 pea 与 sized 复合而成，义为「豌豆大小的」
由 pea 与 soup 复合而成，指用豌豆煮成的浓汤

senses.title: A round green seed grown in a pod
senses.definition: a climbing plant of the legume family, or the round green seed it bears inside a long pod
senses.definitionCN: 豆科的一种攀缘植物，或它结在长豆荚里的绿色圆粒种子
senses.example: Peas need a trellis to climb in a small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 在小菜园里，豌豆需要有个架子才能往上爬。
senses.why: Latin pisum named both the plant and its seed, so the word begins as the name of a crop rather than of a single grain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pisum 兼指这种植物与它的种子，所以这个词最初是作物的名字，而不是单独一粒豆的名字。

senses.title: The seed eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: the seed harvested while still green and soft, cooked as a vegetable or sold frozen and canned
senses.definitionCN: 在仍青嫩时采收的种子，作为蔬菜烹调，或以冷冻、罐装形式出售
senses.example: She added a cup of frozen peas to the rice.
senses.exampleCN: 她往米饭里加了一杯冷冻豌豆。
senses.why: Once the crop reaches the kitchen, the same word names the food on the plate, and the plural is the usual form because peas are eaten in numbers.
senses.whyCN: 当这种作物进了厨房，同一个词就指盘中的食物；因为豌豆总是成把地吃，复数形式反而更常用。

senses.title: A small round object like a pea
senses.definition: any small round thing that resembles a pea in size or shape
senses.definitionCN: 任何在大小或形状上像豌豆的小圆物
senses.example: The beads were the size of peas and just as smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 那些珠子有豌豆大小，也一样光滑。
senses.why: A pea is a ready-made standard of smallness and roundness, so English borrows the vegetable to describe beads, pellets and other tiny spheres.
senses.whyCN: 豌豆是现成的「小而圆」的标准，于是英语借这种蔬菜来描述珠子、小丸等微小的球状物。

intro.en: Pea comes from a Latin name for the pulse, filtered through an Old English form that English later cut in two.
intro.cn: pea 来自拉丁语对这种豆类的称呼，经古英语形式传入，后来又被英语截短成现在的样子。

items.en: Pisum was the Latin name for the pea plant and its seed, and it stands behind most European names for the vegetable.
items.cn: pisum 是拉丁语中对豌豆植株及其种子的称呼，也是欧洲多数语言里这个蔬菜名称的来源。

items.en: Greek pison named the same pulse and is generally thought to come from an older Mediterranean language rather than from Greek itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 pison 指同一种豆类，一般认为它来自更早的地中海语言，而不是希腊语本身。

items.en: Old English borrowed the word as pise or pyse, a singular form that also served as a mass noun for the crop.
items.cn: 古英语借入后写作 pise 或 pyse，这个单数形式同时也当集体名词，指这种作物。

items.en: Middle English used pease for one seed and for many, so speakers began to hear the ending as a plural marker.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pease 兼指一粒和许多粒，于是人们开始把这个词尾听成复数标记。

items.en: English cut the word back to pea as a new singular and formed peas as its plural, a process known as back-formation.
items.cn: 英语把词截短成 pea 作为新的单数，再造出复数 peas，这种过程称为逆构词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the old form of the word, a close compound and two words that merely share its sound; the near-meaning group collects other edible seeds.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的旧形式、一个近亲复合词，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收其他可食用的种子。

entries.definition: The older form of the word, now archaic or dialectal, kept alive in pease pudding.
entries.definitionCN: 这个词的旧形式，现已古旧或限于方言，保留在豌豆泥这一说法里。

entries.definition: The seed of a low plant in the same family, named by joining pea and nut.
entries.definitionCN: 同科矮生植物结的种子，由 pea 与 nut 拼合命名。

entries.definition: A hard round gem formed inside an oyster; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 牡蛎体内形成的坚硬圆珠；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The pointed top of a mountain; only the sound and spelling are close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 山峰的尖顶；只是读音与拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An edible seed of a climbing plant, often kidney-shaped.
entries.definitionCN: 攀缘植物结的可食用种子，常呈肾形。

entries.definition: A small flat seed of a plant in the same family, usually cooked in soup.
entries.definitionCN: 同科植物结的小扁种子，通常煮汤食用。

entries.definition: Any plant that bears pods, or the edible seed of such a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 任何结豆荚的植物，或这类植物的可食用种子。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin seed name that English shortened twice over, so its history is a lesson in how plurals can reshape a singular.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的种子名称，英语先后把它截短了两次，它的历史正好说明复数如何反过来重塑单数。

normal.en: Latin pisum is the oldest recorded name of the seed, and it survives almost unchanged in French pois and Italian pisello.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pisum 是这种种子最早的名称记录，在法语 pois 与意大利语 pisello 里几乎原样保留。

normal.en: English once said pease for one seed and for many, which is why peas now sounds like a plain plural of pea.
normal.cn: 英语曾用 pease 兼指一粒与许多粒，所以今天的 peas 听起来就是 pea 的普通复数。

normal.en: A pea is defined by its pod: the seeds grow in a row inside a long case that splits along one seam.
normal.cn: 豌豆由豆荚来定义：种子成排长在一个长壳里，壳沿着一条缝裂开。

normal.en: Pea green and pea-sized both take the vegetable as a standard of colour and of smallness.
normal.cn: pea green 与 pea-sized 都拿这种蔬菜当作颜色与大小的标准。

normal.en: The noun is countable now, so one says one pea, two peas, and a bowl of peas.
normal.cn: 这个名词现在是可数的，所以说一粒豌豆、两粒豌豆、一碗豌豆。

abstract.en: A pea is a seed that carries its own food and its own case, a small complete package.
abstract.cn: 豌豆是一粒自带养料、自带外壳的种子，一个小而完整的包裹。

abstract.en: The word shrank from pease to pea because speakers rebuilt a singular out of a plural they had misheard.
abstract.cn: 这个词从 pease 缩成 pea，是因为说话人把自己听错的复数重新造成了单数。

abstract.en: Anything small, round and green can be called pea-like, which shows how a vegetable becomes a unit of size.
abstract.cn: 凡是小而圆、颜色发绿的东西都能说成像豌豆，这显示一种蔬菜如何变成大小的单位。

examples.en: She shelled a bowl of peas for dinner.
examples.cn: 她剥了一碗豌豆准备做晚饭。

examples.en: The soup was thick with split peas and ham.
examples.cn: 汤里满是干豌豆和火腿，十分浓稠。

examples.en: Each bead was the size of a pea and smooth as glass.
examples.cn: 每颗珠子都有豌豆大小，光滑得像玻璃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮」——剥开豆荚那层皮，里面就是豌豆；pea 就是豌豆。

root: 来自拉丁语 pisum（豌豆），经古英语 pise、中古英语 pease 演变，近代英语逆构出单数 pea；与表示和平的 peace 只是同音，来源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the seed inside the pod; the senses move from the growing crop to the food on the plate and then to any tiny round thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是豆荚里的种子；义项从地里的作物，移到盘中的食物，再移到任何微小的圆物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thumb pressing the seam of a pod until a row of round seeds rolls into the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指压开豆荚的缝，一排圆豆滚进掌心。

branches.en: a vine climbing a bamboo frame in a kitchen garden
branches.cn: 菜园里顺着竹架往上爬的藤

branches.en: a pod splitting open above a dinner plate
branches.cn: 餐盘上方裂开的豆荚

branches.en: a cup of frozen peas tipped into boiling rice
branches.cn: 一杯冻豌豆倒进沸着的米饭

branches.en: beads rolling across a table, each the size of a seed
branches.cn: 滚过桌面的珠子，颗颗如豆

branches.en: a seed used as a measure for anything very small
branches.cn: 拿豆粒来衡量极细小之物的做法

intro.en: The word comes down from a Latin name for the seed, filtered through an Old English form that English later cut in two.
intro.cn: 这个词源自拉丁语中表示种子的名称，经古英语形式过滤，后来又被英语截成两段。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
