pea, used for one or for many
a dish of boiled split peas

latinEntries.meaning: the pea plant and its seed

definition_zh: 和平；安宁；和睦；和约
definition_en: a state in which there is no war or fighting; also calm and quiet, friendly relations between people, or a treaty that ends a war
core_image: 两双原本握着武器的手松开，掌心向上放在桌上
scene: 战事停下的那个清晨，街上第一次没有枪声，人们推开窗，听见鸟叫。After years of fighting, the two sides finally agreed to make peace.
sceneCN: 这里是「和平」（第 1 个义项：没有战争的状态）；句意是打了多年之后，双方终于同意讲和。画面里有安静的街道、推开的窗与窗外的鸟。

collocations.zh: 处于和平状态；内心平静

derivatives.zh: 由 peace 加形容词词尾 -ful 构成，义为「和平的；宁静的」
由 peace 加 -able 构成，义为「爱好和平的；不爱争执的」
由 peace 与 keeping 复合而成，指以武力或派驻人员维持停火的工作
由 peace 与 time 复合而成，指没有战争的时期

senses.title: Freedom from war
senses.definition: a condition in which nations or groups are not fighting each other
senses.definitionCN: 国家或群体之间不再交战的状态
senses.example: The two countries have lived in peace for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家已经和平相处了五十年。
senses.why: Latin pax named a pact that ended a quarrel, so peace begins as an agreement rather than as a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pax 指结束争执的约定，所以 peace 的起点是一份协议，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Calm and quiet
senses.definition: a state of quiet and calm, free from noise, worry or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 没有噪声、忧虑或打扰的安静平和状态
senses.example: She longed for peace after a day in the noisy market.
senses.exampleCN: 在吵闹的市场待了一天之后，她渴望安宁。
senses.why: The public sense of a stopped war can be felt by one person as a stopped noise, so the word moves inward from the battlefield to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 公共意义上「战争停止」的感受，落实到个人身上就是「噪声停止」，于是这个词从战场转向了内心。

senses.title: Friendly relations between people
senses.definition: a state in which people are not quarrelling and treat each other in a friendly way
senses.definitionCN: 人们不再争吵、彼此以友好方式相处的状态
senses.example: The brothers made peace after a long silence.
senses.exampleCN: 两兄弟在长久互不理睬之后和好了。
senses.why: Scale the same absence of conflict down to a family or a pair of neighbours, and the word still means that nobody is at war.
senses.whyCN: 把同一种「没有冲突」缩小到家庭或两个邻居身上，这个词仍然表示没有人处在交战状态。

senses.title: A treaty that ends a war
senses.definition: an agreement in which two sides formally stop fighting and settle their differences
senses.definitionCN: 双方正式停止交战并解决分歧的协议
senses.example: The peace was signed in a small town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 和约在一座小镇的礼堂里签署。
senses.why: Because pax first meant the agreement itself, the word can name the signed document and not only the state that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pax 最早指协议本身，这个词就能指签署的文件，而不只是协议带来的状态。

intro.en: Peace goes back to a Latin noun for a pact, and it has never lost the idea that peace is something two sides agree to.
intro.cn: peace 可追到拉丁语中表示约定的名词，它始终没有丢掉「和平是双方谈成的事」这一层意思。

items.en: Pax meant a pact or agreement that ended a quarrel, and it also named the state that followed such an agreement.
items.cn: pax 意为结束争执的约定或协议，也指协议达成之后的状态。

items.en: The genitive pacis supplied the stem seen in pacific and pacify, words about making or keeping agreement.
items.cn: 它的属格 pacis 提供了 pacific 与 pacify 所用的词干，这些词都与缔结或维持和约有关。

items.en: Old French pais carried the Latin noun into French with the sense of peace and quiet.
items.cn: 古法语 pais 把这一拉丁名词带入法语，义为和平与安宁。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as pees or pes, and it covered both public peace and personal calm.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 pees 或 pes，既指公共的和平，也指个人的平静。

items.en: Modern English settled on the spelling peace and kept the whole range from treaties to a quiet mind.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 peace，并保留了从和约到内心宁静的整套含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin family of pax and one word that only sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects states of calm and of agreement.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 pax 这一拉丁词族，另加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示平静与意见一致的状态。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between two sides, usually to stop conflict or to cooperate.
entries.definitionCN: 双方达成的正式协议，通常用于停止冲突或开展合作。

entries.definition: Peaceful in intention; also the name of the great ocean.
entries.definitionCN: 意图和平的；也用作大洋的名称。

entries.definition: To calm someone who is angry, or to end fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 使发怒的人平静下来，或平息争斗。

entries.definition: The round green seed eaten as a vegetable; it only sounds like peace, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 作蔬菜食用的绿色圆粒；只是读音与 peace 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A state of being free from worry, movement or noise.
entries.definitionCN: 没有忧虑、动静或噪声的状态。

entries.definition: A state in which people agree and work well together.
entries.definitionCN: 人们意见一致、相处融洽的状态。

entries.definition: An agreement to stop fighting for a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在一定时期内停止交战的协议。

entries.definition: Little or no noise; a still and restful condition.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎没有声响；安静而宜人的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a signed agreement and widens until it can describe a single quiet room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一纸签下的协议出发，一步步扩大，直到能描述一间安静的房间。

normal.en: Pax was a pact, so peace in Latin begins as an agreement rather than as a feeling.
normal.cn: pax 本是一份约定，所以拉丁语里的和平最初是协议，而不是感受。

normal.en: Pacific and pacify share the same stem, which is why all three words are about making or keeping agreement.
normal.cn: pacific 与 pacify 共用同一词干，所以这三个词都与缔结或维持和约有关。

normal.en: English once wrote pees, which is why the modern spelling looks nothing like the Latin pax.
normal.cn: 英语曾把这个词写作 pees，所以今天的拼写与拉丁语 pax 几乎看不出关系。

normal.en: At peace can describe a country and a mind, because the word covers both public and private calm.
normal.cn: at peace 既能说一个国家，也能说一颗心，因为这个词同时覆盖公共与私人的平静。

normal.en: Peace is usually uncountable, but the plural peaces appears when several separate treaties are compared.
normal.cn: peace 通常不可数，但比较几份各自独立的和约时会出现复数 peaces。

abstract.en: Peace is not the absence of anything but the presence of an agreement that both sides intend to keep.
abstract.cn: 和平不是什么东西消失了，而是双方都打算遵守的那份约定还在。

abstract.en: The same word serves a signed treaty and a quiet evening, suggesting that outer order and inner quiet are made of the same material.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既服务于签署的和约，也服务于安静的夜晚，暗示外在秩序与内心安静由同一种材料做成。

abstract.en: A word that began as a handshake now names what whole nations hope for.
abstract.cn: 一个从握手开始的词，如今成了整个国家的愿望。

examples.en: The treaty brought peace to the region after a long war.
examples.cn: 这项条约在长期战事之后为该地区带来了和平。

examples.en: She sat by the window and enjoyed the peace of the early morning.
examples.cn: 她坐在窗边，享受清晨的安宁。

examples.en: The two neighbours finally made peace after months of silence.
examples.cn: 两位邻居在数月互不理睬之后终于和好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮斯」——把武器收起来，世界就安静了；peace 就是和平。

root: 来自拉丁语 pax（和约、和平），属格 pacis，经古法语 pais 进入英语；同族词有 pact、pacific、pacify。与表示豌豆的 pea 只是同音，来源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an agreement that stops a quarrel; the senses run from war between nations, to quiet around a person, to peace between neighbours, and back to the signed treaty itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是让争执停下的约定；义项从国家之间的战争，到人身边的安静，到邻里之间的和睦，最后再回到签署的和约本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands that once held weapons opening and resting flat on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双原本握着武器的手松开，掌心向上放在桌上。

branches.en: a morning when the guns finally fall silent
branches.cn: 枪声终于停下的清晨

branches.en: a quiet window opened to birdsong
branches.cn: 推开窗户听见鸟叫的安静时刻

branches.en: two brothers shaking hands after a long silence
branches.cn: 两兄弟在长久沉默后握的手

branches.en: a treaty signed on a plain wooden desk
branches.cn: 在朴素木桌上签署的和约

branches.en: one word holding a nation, a room and a friendship
branches.cn: 一个词同时托住国家、房间与友情

intro.en: A Latin noun of agreement, its oblique stem and a French reshaping hold the word together, with -ful and -able branching off it.
intro.cn: 一个表示约定的拉丁名词、它的斜格词干以及法语的重塑共同支撑这个词，-ful 与 -able 又从它分出新的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the work of keeping a truce

definition_zh: 教育学；教学法；关于教学与学习方法的理论与实践
definition_en: the theory and practice of teaching
core_image: 一位老师把整间教室的桌椅重新摆成半圆，让每个孩子都能看见别人的眼睛，再开始提问
scene: 师范学院的课堂上，学生先设计一堂课，再互相扮演学生，最后拆解刚才每一步为什么有效。The seminar examined pedagogy by having students teach a lesson and then dissect it.
sceneCN: 这里 pedagogy 指关于教学方法的理论与实践（第 1 个义项：教学的艺术与学问）；句意为研讨课让学生先上一堂课，再拆解它，以此来考察教学法。

pos.zh: 教育学；教学法（不可数，指理论、学问或方法体系）
某一教师或某一学科的教学风格与做法

collocations.zh: 评价方式背后的教学观

derivatives.zh: 教师；（贬义）教书匠（由希腊语「护送男孩的家奴」经拉丁与法语进入英语，从照看孩子的人转指教师）
教学法的（由希腊语「教学」词干加表示「属于」的希腊后缀构成，经拉丁与法语进入英语）
教学法的；教育学的（由 pedagogic 加表示「属于」的英语后缀构成）
从教学法角度（由 pedagogical 加表示「方式」的后缀构成）
教学法研究（由 pedagogic 加表示「学问」的后缀构成，指教学法的系统研究）

senses.title: The art and science of teaching
senses.definition: the study and practice of how teaching is done, treated as both a craft and a field of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 对教学如何进行的学问与实践，既被视为技艺，也被视为知识领域
senses.example: The seminar examined pedagogy by having students teach a lesson and then dissect it.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课让学生先上一堂课，再拆解它，以此来考察教学法。
senses.why: The Greek word first named the slave who led a boy to school; the modern word names the study of that leading, now done by teachers themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初命名送男孩上学的家奴；现代词则命名对「引导」这件事的研究，如今由教师自己来做。

senses.title: The theory of instruction
senses.definition: a systematic account of how instruction should be designed and why it works
senses.definitionCN: 关于教学应当如何设计、为何有效的系统论述
senses.example: Her book sets out a pedagogy grounded in how novices actually think.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书提出一种以初学者实际如何思考为基础的教学理论。
senses.why: Theory turns practice into something that can be argued about, tested and taught to new teachers.
senses.whyCN: 理论把实践变成可争论、可检验、可教给新教师的东西。

senses.title: The method or practice of teaching
senses.definition: the concrete choices a teacher makes in a classroom, such as grouping, questioning and pacing
senses.definitionCN: 教师在课堂上做出的具体选择，如分组、提问与节奏
senses.example: His pedagogy changed when he moved the desks into a circle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把课桌摆成圆形后，教学法也随之改变。
senses.why: Here the word is closest to practice: it names what a teacher actually does, not what a journal article recommends.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词最贴近实践：它命名教师实际怎么做，而非期刊论文建议怎么做。

senses.title: Critical pedagogy
senses.definition: an approach that treats teaching as a way of questioning power and inviting students to act
senses.definitionCN: 把教学视为质疑权力、邀请学生行动的一种路径
senses.example: Critical pedagogy asks whose knowledge the textbook leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 批判教育学追问教科书漏掉了谁的知识。
senses.why: A named school within the field, it joins the word to a political commitment rather than to technique alone.
senses.whyCN: 这是领域内部一个有名字的流派，它把教学法与政治承诺结合，而非只与技术结合。

senses.title: The pedagogy of the oppressed
senses.definition: a teaching practice that begins from the experience of the oppressed and aims at their liberation
senses.definitionCN: 从受压迫者的经验出发、以其解放为目标的教学实践
senses.example: The course read the pedagogy of the oppressed alongside folk-school records.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程把受压迫者教育学与民间学校档案并读。
senses.why: The phrase turns teaching into a political act, so pedagogy here is not neutral method but a stance.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把教学变成政治行动，因此这里的教学法不是中立方法，而是一种立场。

senses.title: Subject-specific pedagogy
senses.definition: the particular ways of teaching a subject, such as history pedagogy or mathematics pedagogy
senses.definitionCN: 教授某一学科的特有方式，如历史教学法或数学教学法
senses.example: Mathematics pedagogy has its own debates about symbols and proof.
senses.exampleCN: 数学教学法有自己关于符号与证明的争论。
senses.why: Each discipline has its own ways of making knowledge visible, so the word attaches to the subject.
senses.whyCN: 每门学科都有让知识可见的特有方式，因此这个词会接上具体学科。

senses.title: Curriculum design as pedagogy
senses.titleCN: 课程设计层面的教学法
senses.definition: the arrangement of content, sequence and assessment understood as part of teaching rather than as administration
senses.definitionCN: 把内容、顺序与评价的安排理解为教学的一部分，而非行政事务
senses.example: The new curriculum was praised for its pedagogy, not its list of topics.
senses.exampleCN: 新课程受到称赞的是它的教学安排，而不是主题清单。
senses.why: Design carries teaching: what is placed first and what is tested tells students what kind of learning is expected.
senses.whyCN: 设计本身承载教学：先放什么、考什么，都在告诉学生期待何种学习。

senses.title: Abstract: shaping of learning
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对学习的有意塑造
senses.definition: any deliberate arrangement that shapes how someone learns, inside or outside a classroom
senses.definitionCN: 任何有意安排、塑造某人如何学习的方式，无论课堂内外
senses.example: A good museum label has its own pedagogy.
senses.exampleCN: 一块好的博物馆说明牌也有自己的教学法。
senses.why: At its widest the word names the intention behind an arrangement, not a profession or a syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个词命名安排背后的意图，而非职业或大纲。

intro.en: Pedagogy comes from Greek paidagogia, 'attendance on a boy', built on pais 'child' and agein 'to lead'. The modern sense of theory of teaching is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pedagogy 来自希腊语 paidagogia「照看男孩」，由 pais「孩子」与 agein「引导」构成。现代「教学理论」义要晚得多。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pais, with the stem paid-, meant 'child, boy'. The same stem appears in pediatrics, the care of children.
items.cn: pais 的词干是 paid-，意为「孩子、男孩」。同一词干也出现在 pediatrics（儿科）中。

items.en: Agein meant 'to lead, drive'. It supplies the second half of the word and the idea of guiding someone.
items.cn: agein 意为「引导、驱赶」。它提供这个词的后半段与「引导某人」的意象。

items.en: Paidagogos named the household slave who escorted a boy to school and supervised him on the way. The word named a person, not a theory.
items.cn: paidagogos 指护送男孩上学、沿途照看的家奴。这个词命名的是人，不是理论。

items.en: Paidagogia meant 'attendance on a boy', the work of that slave. In ancient Greek it did not mean the theory of teaching.
items.cn: paidagogia 意为「照看男孩」，是那个家奴的工作。在古希腊语中，它不指教学理论。

items.en: Latin borrowed paedagogus and paedagogia, and French pédagogie carried the word into educational writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 paedagogus 与 paedagogia，法语 pédagogie 把这个词带进教育写作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): English pedagogy is recorded from the sixteenth century, but the modern sense of the theory of teaching became common only later.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语 pedagogy 自十六世纪有记录，但「教学理论」这一现代义后来才通行。

note.en: Group one separates the word from its relative for the teacher and from two Greek look-alikes; group two holds the near names for teaching as a field.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与指教师的亲属词、以及两个希腊语形近词分开；第二组是把教学作为领域的近邻名称。

entries.definition: The teacher; the noun for the person, while pedagogy names the theory or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 教师；这个名词指人，而 pedagogy 指理论或实践。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching methods; the adjective describes what pedagogy names.
entries.definitionCN: 与教学方法有关的；形容词描述 pedagogy 所命名的东西。

entries.definition: From pais 'child' plus iatreia 'healing'; it shares the child stem but has nothing to do with teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pais「孩子」加 iatreia「治疗」构成；它共享「孩子」词干，却与教学无关。

entries.definition: From dēmos 'people' plus agein 'lead': leading the people by appeal to emotion. It shares agein but not pais.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dēmos「人民」加 agein「引导」构成：以情绪诉求引导民众。它共享 agein，却不共享 pais。

entries.definition: The everyday name for the activity; pedagogy adds theory, method and reflection.
entries.definitionCN: 这项活动的日常名称；pedagogy 加上理论、方法与反思。

entries.definition: The act of delivering lessons or directions; it stresses transmission more than pedagogy does.
entries.definitionCN: 传递课程或指令的行为；它比 pedagogy 更强调传递。

entries.definition: The study of teaching methods, from Greek didaskein 'to teach'; it overlaps with pedagogy but is often narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 对教学方法的研究，来自希腊语 didaskein「教」；与 pedagogy 重叠，但通常更窄。

entries.definition: The broad process and system of educating; pedagogy is the teaching side of it, not the whole institution.
entries.definitionCN: 教育的广义过程与制度；pedagogy 是其中教学的一面，而非整个制度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real Greek words and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的希腊词与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pais means child, so pedagogy begins with the young person being led.
normal.cn: pais 意为孩子，所以 pedagogy 从被引导的年轻人开始。

normal.en: Agein means lead, so the second half is the act of guiding, not filling.
normal.cn: agein 意为引导，所以后半段是引导的动作，不是填充。

normal.en: The ancient paidagogos was a slave escort, which is why the word first named a person rather than a method.
normal.cn: 古代的 paidagogos 是护送的家奴，所以这个词最初命名人，而非方法。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the schools: critical pedagogy, subject pedagogy, classroom pedagogy.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出流派：批判教育学、学科教学法、课堂教学法。

normal.en: Pediatrics shares pais but not agein, so it is about children's health, not teaching.
normal.cn: pediatrics 共享 pais 却不共享 agein，所以它关乎儿童健康，与教学无关。

abstract.en: Picture a room rearranged into a half circle so every child can see every other child's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子被摆成半圆，让每个孩子都能看见别人的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a lesson taken apart on a table like a clock, each step laid beside the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一堂课像钟表一样被拆在桌上，每一步都摆在下一步旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp carried ahead of a small figure on a dark road to school.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯在暗路上走在一个小身影前面，通往学校。

examples.en: The department treats pedagogy as a research field, not as a set of tricks.
examples.cn: 这个系把教学法当作研究领域，而非一套窍门。

examples.en: Her pedagogy gives students time to be wrong before they are corrected.
examples.cn: 她的教学法给学生留出犯错的时间，再加以纠正。

examples.en: The report compares the pedagogy of online and face-to-face courses.
examples.cn: 报告比较在线课程与面授课程的教学法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派达 够 吉」——牵着孩子走向学堂的那门学问 → 教学法

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with teaching as a craft and a field, then move to theory, classroom practice, critical schools, liberation, subject methods, curriculum design and finally any deliberate shaping of learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把教学看作技艺与领域，再转到理论、课堂实践、批判流派、解放、学科方法、课程设计，最后是任何对学习的有意塑造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp carried ahead of a child on the road to school, then the same road studied by teachers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯在孩子上学的路上走在前头，随后这条路由教师来研究。

branches.en: CRAFT AND CLASSROOM: teaching as knowledge, then as the concrete choices made in a room.
branches.cn: 技艺与课堂：教学作为知识，再作为课堂中的具体选择。

branches.en: THEORY: instruction explained systematically so that it can be argued and tested.
branches.cn: 理论：对教学作系统解释，使其可被争论与检验。

branches.en: CRITICAL AND LIBERATING: named schools that make teaching a political stance.
branches.cn: 批判与解放：有名字的流派，把教学变成政治立场。

branches.en: SUBJECT AND SEQUENCE: methods specific to a discipline, and design as a form of teaching.
branches.cn: 学科与顺序：特定学科的方法，以及作为教学形式的设计。

branches.en: THE INTENTION: any arrangement that deliberately shapes how someone learns.
branches.cn: 意图：任何有意塑造某人如何学习的安排。

intro.en: Pedagogy is Greek from top to bottom: a child, a leader and the slave who walked between them.
intro.cn: pedagogy 从头到尾都是希腊语：一个孩子、一位引导者，以及走在两者之间的家奴。

latinIntro.en: Greek pais and agein build paidagogos and paidagogia; English adds pedagogy, pedagogue and pedagogical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 pais 与 agein 构成 paidagogos 与 paidagogia；英语再加 pedagogy、pedagogue 与 pedagogical。

definition_zh: 处罚；惩罚；处以罚款；扣分；判罚；使处于不利地位
definition_en: to impose a punishment or a disadvantage on someone because of a fault or an advantage they hold
core_image: 记分员在犯规者名字后面添上一笔扣减，把他刚挣来的领先一点点抹掉
scene: 赛季审查时，委员会发现一支车队在测试中用了超标的引擎，于是决定扣掉它上一站挣得的积分。The committee penalized the team by deducting the points it had won at the previous race.
sceneCN: 这里指「以扣分的方式处罚」，对应第 3 个义项：把已经获得的分数部分或全部扣除；句意为委员会因引擎违规而扣掉了该车队上一站赢得的积分。画面要点：审查报告、积分表、被划掉的那几行数字。

pos.zh: 处罚；使处于不利地位（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明原因）

collocations.zh: 使小企业处于不利地位
对提前还款收取违约金

derivatives.zh: 由 penalize 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「被处罚的过程或状态」
由 penalize 加过去分词后缀 → 由「施加处罚」转为形容「已经受罚的」
由 penalize 加现在分词后缀 → 由「施加处罚」转为形容「带有惩罚性质、正在造成不利的」
去掉动词后缀，回到形容词词干（拉丁 poenalis）→ 由「施加处罚的动作」回到「与刑罚有关的性质」
去掉动词后缀，换上名词后缀（经古法语与拉丁语，表性质）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「所施加的那份处罚」

senses.title: To punish under a rule
senses.titleCN: 依规则对违规者施加处罚
senses.definition: to impose a declared punishment on someone who has broken a rule
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则的人施加事先声明的惩罚
senses.example: The referee penalized the forward for a deliberate handball.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因前锋故意手球而判罚了他。
senses.why: The suffix -ize turns the noun of punishment into an action, so the word names the moment a rule is enforced against a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词后缀把「处罚」这个名词变成动作，于是这个词指的就是规则落到某人身上的那一刻。

senses.title: To impose a fine
senses.definition: to require an offender to pay a sum of money as the punishment
senses.definitionCN: 要求违规者缴纳一笔钱作为惩罚
senses.example: The city penalizes owners who fail to clear snow from the pavement.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府对未清除人行道积雪的业主处以罚款。
senses.why: Because the noun behind the verb could mean a sum of money, the action can be carried out with a receipt and a payment deadline.
senses.whyCN: 因为动词背后的名词本就可以指一笔钱，所以这个动作可以用一张收据和一个缴款期限来完成。

senses.title: To strip points or a result
senses.titleCN: 扣除已获得的分数或成绩
senses.definition: to deduct points, a win or a record that someone has already gained
senses.definitionCN: 把某人已经取得的分数、胜场或纪录扣除
senses.example: The committee penalized the team by deducting the points it had won at the previous race.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会扣掉了该车队上一站赢得的积分，以示处罚。
senses.why: When the punishment is counted in points rather than money, the same verb simply takes away what the scoreboard already holds.
senses.whyCN: 当惩罚以分数而不是钱来计算，同一个动词所做的就是拿走记分牌上已有的东西。

senses.title: To handicap a player in sport
senses.titleCN: 在比赛中判罚或加罚某位选手
senses.definition: to place a sporting disadvantage on a player or team for an infringement
senses.definitionCN: 因违规而把某项体育上的不利加给选手或球队
senses.example: Golfers are penalized two strokes when the ball goes out of bounds.
senses.exampleCN: 球出界时，高尔夫球手会被加罚两杆。
senses.why: The penalty in sport is not paid to anyone; it is carried by the offender, so the verb shifts from collecting a debt to loading a burden.
senses.whyCN: 体育中的罚并不是付给谁的，而是由犯规者自己背着；于是这个动词从「收取代价」转为「给身上加负担」。

senses.title: To make a group bear a cost
senses.titleCN: 让某一群体承担额外成本
senses.definition: to arrange rules or charges so that a particular group carries a heavier burden
senses.definitionCN: 使规则或收费安排让某一群体承担更重的负担
senses.example: The tax penalizes families with a single earner.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税使单收入家庭处于不利地位。
senses.why: Once the verb means 'load a burden on', no offence is needed: a policy itself can penalize by loading one group more heavily than another.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个动词意为「给身上加负担」，就不需要有人违规：一项政策只要让某一群体背得更重，就已经在「罚」它了。

senses.title: To forbid by attaching a sanction
senses.titleCN: 以处罚为后盾禁止某种行为
senses.definition: to attach a legal sanction to a practice so that those who repeat it are punished
senses.definitionCN: 为某种行为附加法律制裁，使继续做的人受到惩罚
senses.example: The new code penalizes the dumping of waste in rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 新法典对向河流倾倒废弃物的行为规定了处罚。
senses.why: A law that threatens punishment is written in the same verb: the action is not yet punished, but the sanction already stands behind the ban.
senses.whyCN: 一条以惩罚相威胁的法律也用同一个动词来写：行为尚未受罚，但制裁已经立在禁令背后。

senses.title: To punish a group for one member's act
senses.titleCN: 因一人之过而连带处罚整组人
senses.definition: to make several people suffer for the fault of a single member among them
senses.definitionCN: 因群体中某一个人的过错而让多个人一起承担后果
senses.example: The coach penalized the whole squad for one player's lateness.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因一名球员迟到而处罚了整支队伍。
senses.why: If punishment can be assigned by rule rather than by blame, it can also be spread across a group, whether or not each member took part.
senses.whyCN: 如果处罚可以按规则指派而不必按罪责指派，它也能摊到一整组人身上，无论每个人是否参与。

senses.title: To treat unfairly through a built-in bias
senses.titleCN: 因规则自带的偏见而使人吃亏
senses.definition: to place a particular kind of person at a disadvantage through rules that do not name them openly
senses.definitionCN: 通过并未明指某类人的规则，使这类人处于劣势
senses.example: The old rules penalized women who took career breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 旧规则使中断职业发展的女性吃亏。
senses.why: A burden can fall on a whole category of people without any fault at all, and at that point the verb shades into unfair treatment.
senses.whyCN: 负担可以毫无过错地落在整整一类人身上，到了这一步，这个动词就带上「不公平对待」的色彩。

intro.en: Penalize is an English construction rather than a Latin inheritance: the adjective penal, from Latin poenalis, plus the verb suffix -ize. It appeared in the nineteenth century, when English began to form verbs freely from adjectives. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: penalize 是英语自身的构造，而不是直接承自拉丁：它由拉丁 poenalis 而来的形容词 penal 加动词后缀构成，出现于十九世纪，正值英语开始大量由形容词造动词的时期。年代均为约数。

items.en: Poena named punishment and the compensation that settled a wrong, and it is the ultimate source of the whole family.
items.cn: poena 指处罚以及为平息过错而付的补偿，是整个词族的最初源头。

items.en: The adjective poenalis 'of punishment' passed through French as penal into English, keeping the descriptive sense.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 意为「与处罚有关的」，经法语作 penal 进入英语，保留了描述性质的意思。

items.en: English penal described laws, codes and systems of punishment, so the stem was ready to take an action suffix.
items.cn: 英语的 penal 用来描述法律、法典与惩罚体系，这个词干已经准备好接上一个表动作的后缀。

items.en: The suffix -ize, from French -iser and Latin -izare, turns an adjective into a verb meaning 'to make or to act in that way'.
items.cn: 动词后缀经法语与拉丁语而来，把形容词变成意为「使之成为或按此行事」的动词。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the nineteenth century, when rules, taxes and games all needed a word for the act of laying a penalty on someone.
items.cn: 这个动词首见于十九世纪，当时规则、税制与比赛都需要一个词来指「把处罚加到某人身上」这一动作。

items.en: Twentieth-century usage widened it from legal punishment to any rule, fee or bias that leaves one side worse off.
items.cn: 二十世纪的用法把它从法律惩罚扩展到任何使某一方更吃亏的规则、收费或偏见。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin stem and one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of imposing a burden.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「施加负担」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The adjective from which the verb is built; it names the character of a measure rather than the act of applying it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词所由构成的形容词；它指一项措施的性质，而不是施加这一动作。

entries.definition: The noun naming what is imposed; the verb names the imposing, so the pair look alike but differ in grammatical role.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加之物的名词；动词则指施加动作，两者形近而语法角色不同。

entries.definition: An adjective from Latin punire meaning 'intended to punish'; it describes purpose, not the act of applying a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 而来的形容词，意为「意在惩罚的」；它描述目的，而不描述执行规则的动作。

entries.definition: A flat board or a group of experts; it merely looks like penalize in spelling and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一块平板或一组专家；只是拼写与 penalize 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To make someone suffer for a wrong; it stresses the pain inflicted, while penalize stresses the rule or the disadvantage.
entries.definitionCN: 因过错而使人受苦；它强调施加的痛苦，而 penalize 强调规则或不利处境。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour by training or punishment; it carries the aim of reform, which penalize does not require.
entries.definitionCN: 以训练或惩罚纠正行为；它带着「改正」的目的，而 penalize 并不要求这一点。

entries.definition: To charge a sum of money as punishment; it covers one sense of penalize and nothing more.
entries.definitionCN: 以收取一笔钱作为处罚；它只覆盖 penalize 的一个义项，别无其他。

entries.definition: To put someone in a worse position; it captures the burden sense but leaves out the rule and the fault.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人处于更差的位置；它抓住「负担」这一层，却不含规则与过错。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real adjective it comes from and the real related nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、构成它的真实形容词，以及真实的同族名词。

normal.en: Penalize is penal plus -ize, so it means 'to make penal', to turn a rule into an actual burden.
normal.cn: penalize 是 penal 加动词后缀，意思是「使带有惩罚」，把一条规则变成真实的负担。

normal.en: Everything in this family goes back to poena, the Latin price of a wrong.
normal.cn: 这一词族里的一切都可上溯到 poena，即拉丁语中「过错的代价」。

normal.en: Penalize usually names who suffers and why: penalize a team for cheating, penalize drivers for speeding.
normal.cn: penalize 通常点明谁受损与为何受损：因作弊处罚球队，因超速处罚司机。

normal.en: Pair it with its noun to feel the difference: the noun names what is imposed, the verb names who is made to carry it.
normal.cn: 把它与同族名词配对来体会差别：名词说的是被施加的那项处罚，动词说的是让谁去承担这项处罚。

normal.en: No fault is needed in the modern sense; a tax or a deadline can penalize you simply by costing you more.
normal.cn: 现代义里不必有人犯错；一项税或一个截止期限，只要让你多付，就已经在「罚」你。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on one side of a balance while the other side rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把天平的一端往下按，另一端就翘了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard where a small eraser rubs out two lines the moment a whistle blows.
abstract.cn: 想象哨声一响，一块小橡皮就在记分牌上擦掉两行数字。

abstract.en: Picture a runner carrying a sandbag that nobody else in the race was given.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者背着一只沙袋，而赛道上其他人都没有分到。

examples.en: The board penalized the firm for filing a false report.
examples.cn: 董事会因该公司的虚假报告而对其作出处罚。

examples.en: Rules that penalize part-time students keep many adults out of college.
examples.cn: 使非全日制学生吃亏的规则，把许多成年人挡在大学门外。

examples.en: He was penalized ten seconds for blocking another skier.
examples.cn: 他因阻挡另一名滑雪者而被加罚十秒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈了来宰」——一刀劈下去再宰一刀，违规者被一层层扣罚 → 处罚、扣分

root: 拉丁 poena「处罚、补偿」→ 拉丁形容词 poenalis → 法语 penal → 英语形容词 penal → 加动词后缀 → penalize「把处罚加到某人身上」；同族词有 penalty、punish、punitive。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses are one act seen from different angles: a burden is placed on someone. The burden may follow a broken rule, take the shape of money, remove points, handicap a player, fall on a group, stand behind a ban, cover a whole squad, or follow from a rule's hidden bias.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个动作的不同侧面：把一份负担加到某人身上。这份负担可以因违规而来、以钱的形式出现、扣走分数、加在选手身上、落到某个群体、立在禁令背后、摊到整支队伍，或来自规则里隐藏的偏见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scorer adding a deduction behind an offender's name and rubbing out the lead just earned.
core.cn: 核心意象：记分员在犯规者的名字后面添上一笔扣减，把刚挣来的领先擦掉。

branches.en: ENFORCEMENT: the rule is applied to a person, either as a declared punishment or as a sum of money.
branches.cn: 执行：规则落到具体的人身上，或表现为声明的处罚，或表现为一笔钱。

branches.en: SCORE AND SPORT: what was already gained is taken away, or a stroke is added on the field.
branches.cn: 分数与赛场：已经拿到的东西被拿走，或在场上多加一杆。

branches.en: STRUCTURAL COST: rules and charges can load one group more heavily without any offence.
branches.cn: 结构性成本：规则与收费可以不经任何过错，就把某一群体压得更重。

branches.en: SANCTION ATTACHED: a ban is written with its punishment already standing behind it.
branches.cn: 附加制裁：一条禁令在写下的同时，惩罚已经立在它背后。

branches.en: SPREAD AND BIAS: the burden reaches a whole squad, or quietly falls on a category of people.
branches.cn: 扩散与偏见：负担扩到整支队伍，或悄然落在某一类人身上。

intro.en: Penalize is a transparent English build: a Latin-derived adjective plus a verb suffix, with the Latin noun still visible underneath.
intro.cn: penalize 是构造透明的英语词：一个源自拉丁的形容词加一个动词后缀，底下的拉丁名词仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun poena and its adjective poenalis sit under penal, penalty and penalize, while the Latin verb punire underlies punish and punitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 poena 及其形容词 poenalis 位于 penal、penalty 与 penalize 之下，而拉丁动词 punire 则位于 punish 与 punitive 之下。

items.example: The stem is hidden but still present in the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干虽被遮住，却仍在词里。

items.example: The penal system was under review.
items.exampleCN: 惩罚体系正在接受审查。

items.meaning: to make or to act in the stated way
items.meaningCN: 使成为或按所说的方式行事
items.example: The suffix turns adjectives into verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成动词。
法规对逾期付款予以处罚。
受罚的公司提出了申诉。
一项惩罚性关税伤害了消费者。

items.example: The penalization of whistle-blowers drew criticism.
items.exampleCN: 对举报人的处罚引来批评。

items.example: The penalty was doubled on appeal.

items.structure: Latin punire through Old French punir
items.meaning: to make suffer for a wrong

items.exampleCN: 法院判给了惩罚性赔偿。

definition_zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚；（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆；不利后果；代价
definition_en: a punishment or disadvantage imposed for breaking a rule, failing a standard, or gaining an unfair advantage
core_image: 裁判在记分牌上划掉犯规一方的一分，再让对方站到更有利的位置上
scene: 足球场上，后卫在禁区里从背后绊倒对方前锋，裁判指向点球点，并向犯规者出示黄牌。The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
sceneCN: 这里指「体育比赛中因犯规而判给对方的一次罚球」，对应第 4 个义项：犯规之后由对方在固定位置主罚的一脚；句意为后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。画面要点：禁区线、点球点、裁判手中的黄牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚（可数，常与 impose、pay、face 连用）
（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆（可数，足球、橄榄球、高尔夫常用）

derivatives.zh: 与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经形容词 poenalis 进入英语 → 由「那笔罚」转为形容「与刑罚有关的性质」
由 penal 加动词后缀（经法语与拉丁语，表「使……化」）→ 语义由「属于刑罚的」转为「施加处罚这一动作」
由 penalize 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「被处罚的过程或状态」
penalty 加复数后缀 → 由一次处罚转为多起、多类处罚
与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经动词 punire 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「罚金」转为「以惩罚为目的、带有惩罚性质的」

senses.title: A punishment for a breach
senses.titleCN: 因违反规则而受的处罚
senses.definition: a punishment imposed on a person or group that has broken a rule or failed a duty
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则或未尽义务的个人与团体所施加的惩罚
senses.example: The league imposed a heavy penalty on the club for breaching the salary cap.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟因该俱乐部违反工资上限而对其处以重罚。
senses.why: Latin poena named the price exacted after a wrong, so the word begins as the consequence that follows a fault, not as the fault itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 指犯错之后被索取的代价，所以这个词从一开始就是过错之后随之而来的后果，而不是过错本身。

senses.title: Money exacted for an offence
senses.titleCN: 为违法行为缴纳的钱款
senses.definition: a sum of money that an offender is required to pay to the authority that recorded the offence
senses.definitionCN: 违法者必须向记录该行为的机关缴纳的一笔钱
senses.example: Drivers face a penalty of two hundred pounds for using a phone at the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 司机开车时使用手机，将面临两百英镑的罚款。
senses.why: Since poena also meant the compensation handed over to settle a wrong, the abstract consequence could be counted out in coins.
senses.whyCN: 因为 poena 也指为平息过错而交出的补偿，这种抽象的后果便可以用钱币数出来。

senses.title: A punishment fixed in statute
senses.definition: the punishment that a law prescribes for a particular offence, usually stated as a maximum
senses.definitionCN: 法律为某一具体罪行规定的惩罚，通常以最高刑期或最高数额表述
senses.example: The statute carries a maximum penalty of ten years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 该法条规定的最高刑罚是十年监禁。
senses.why: When a community writes the price of a wrong into a code, the word shifts from the verdict spoken in court to the number printed in the law book.
senses.whyCN: 当共同体把过错的代价写进法典，这个词就从法庭上宣读的判决，转为法律文本里印着的那个数目。

senses.title: A free shot awarded for a foul
senses.titleCN: 因犯规而判给对方的罚球
senses.definition: an advantage given to the opposing side in a sport because the other side broke a rule
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛中因一方犯规而判给另一方的有利机会
senses.example: The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal word because a foul must be paid for; here the payment takes the form of an unopposed shot from a marked spot.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律用词，因为犯规必须付出代价；在这里，代价的形式是在固定点上无人防守的一脚射门。

senses.title: A stroke added in golf
senses.titleCN: 高尔夫中被加罚的一杆
senses.definition: an extra stroke added to a player's score as a punishment for a mistake on the course
senses.definitionCN: 球场上因失误而被加进球员成绩里的一杆
senses.example: His ball found the water, so he took a penalty and dropped again.
senses.exampleCN: 他的球落进水里，于是他接受罚杆后重新抛球。
senses.why: Golf counts strokes instead of money, so paying for a mistake means adding a stroke to your own card.
senses.whyCN: 高尔夫数的是杆数而不是钱，所以为失误付出代价，就是在自己的记分卡上多加一杆。

senses.title: A charge for breaking a contract
senses.titleCN: 违反合同条款应付的违约金
senses.definition: an amount that a contract requires one party to pay if it acts in a way the agreement forbids
senses.definitionCN: 合同要求一方在做出协议禁止的行为时支付的款项
senses.example: Early repayment of the loan triggers a penalty of one month's interest.
senses.exampleCN: 提前偿还贷款会触发相当于一个月利息的违约金。
senses.why: A contract fixes in advance what a breach will cost, turning the older idea of compensation into a clause with a stated figure.
senses.whyCN: 合同事先定明违约要花多少钱，把较早的「补偿」观念变成一条写着具体数目的条款。

senses.title: The price of an advantage
senses.definition: a disadvantage that comes with a privilege or a success rather than with a rule broken
senses.definitionCN: 伴随特权或成功而来的不利之处，而不是因违规招致的
senses.example: Fame brought her the penalty of constant scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 名气给她带来了被人时刻审视的代价。
senses.why: If every gain carries a price, then even a privilege can carry a penalty, although no rule has been broken.
senses.whyCN: 如果每一种获得都带着价码，那么连特权也能带上「罚」，尽管并没有谁违规。

senses.title: A handicap laid on a contestant
senses.titleCN: 加在参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.definition: a disadvantage imposed on a competitor in order to equalize unequal starting points
senses.definitionCN: 为使不相等的起跑条件趋于平衡而加在某位参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.example: The older runners started with a time penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的跑者带着时间上的不利条件起跑。
senses.why: Any contest that tries to balance unequal starting points can turn punishment into a handicap placed on the stronger side.
senses.whyCN: 凡是试图平衡起跑差距的比赛，都能把「罚」变成加在占优一方身上的不利条件。

intro.en: Penalty comes from Latin poena 'penalty, punishment, compensation', itself a loan from Greek poine 'price paid for a wrong'. Through Old French penalite it entered English law. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: penalty 出自拉丁语 poena「处罚、惩罚、补偿」，而 poena 又借自希腊语 poine「为过错付出的代价」；它经古法语 penalite 进入英语法律用语。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Poine named the price that settled a wrong, whether blood-money paid to a family or a fine owed to a community.
items.cn: poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，既可以是赔给家族的偿命钱，也可以是交给共同体的罚金。

items.en: Poena kept both halves of that idea: the punishment itself and the sum handed over in compensation.
items.cn: poena 保留了这个观念的两半：处罚本身，以及作为补偿交出的那笔钱。

items.en: The adjective poenalis 'of punishment' produced English penal and later supplied the stem for penalize.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 意为「与处罚有关的」，它生成英语的 penal，后来又提供了 penalize 的词干。

items.en: Legal French used penalite for the punishment attached to an offence, and Middle English took the word in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法律法语用 penalite 指附在某一罪行上的处罚，中古英语在十五世纪吸收了这个词。

items.en: Penalty first named a punishment in law, then any sum exacted, then any disadvantage fixed by an agreement.
items.cn: penalty 最初指法律上的处罚，随后指任何被索取的钱款，再后来指协议定下的任何不利后果。

items.en: Nineteenth-century football rules turned the word into the name of the kick itself, and golf gave it the sense of an added stroke.
items.cn: 十九世纪的足球规则把这个词变成那脚罚球本身的名称，高尔夫又赋予它「加罚一杆」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the same Latin stem plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for a punishment or a burden.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「处罚或负担」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of punishment'; it describes the legal character of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「刑罚的」的形容词；它描述一项措施的惩罚性质，而不指这项措施本身。

entries.definition: The verb built on penal; it names the act of imposing what a penalty names as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 penal 构成的动词；penalty 指那件被施加的罚，这个动词则指施加的动作。

entries.definition: Formed from Latin punire rather than directly from poena; it stresses the intention to punish.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁动词 punire 而非直接由 poena 构成；它强调「意在惩罚」这一层。

entries.definition: A small room where food is kept; it merely looks like penalty in spelling and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 存放食物的小房间；只是拼写与 penalty 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: A sum paid as punishment for an offence; it covers the money sense but not the sporting or contractual ones.
entries.definitionCN: 因违法而缴纳的一笔钱；它只覆盖金钱义，不覆盖体育与合同义。

entries.definition: A penalty applied by an authority to enforce a rule; broader in politics and diplomacy, narrower in sport.
entries.definitionCN: 权威为执行规则而施加的处罚；在政治与外交中范围更广，在体育中范围更窄。

entries.definition: Something lost by rule because of a fault; it stresses what is taken away rather than what is imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 因过错而按规则失去的东西；它强调被拿走的东西，而不是被施加的东西。

entries.definition: A disadvantage placed on a stronger competitor; it matches the sporting sense but carries no blame.
entries.definitionCN: 加在较强竞争者身上的不利条件；与体育义相合，但不含责备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的派生词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Poena is the Latin word for the price of a wrong; a penalty is that price written down.
normal.cn: poena 是拉丁语中「过错的代价」，penalty 就是把这笔代价写下来。

normal.en: The same family runs through penal, penalize and punitive, all keeping the idea of a price to be paid.
normal.cn: 同一词族贯穿 penal、penalize 与 punitive，都保留「要付代价」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases lock the senses: death penalty, penalty kick, penalty clause.
normal.cn: 固定搭配锁定义项：死刑、点球、违约金条款。

normal.en: A penalty is always owed to someone: a referee, a court or a contract.
normal.cn: 罚总是欠着某一方的：裁判、法庭或合同。

normal.en: If no rule was broken and nothing is owed, there is no penalty.
normal.cn: 若无人违规、无所亏欠，就谈不上罚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin box beside a rulebook, and every broken rule drops a coin in.
abstract.cn: 想象规则手册旁放着一只钱箱，每破一条规则就投进一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a runner made to stand two steps behind the line because he started too early.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者因为抢跑，被要求站到起跑线后两步。

abstract.en: Picture a hill of trophies with a small toll gate at the foot, charging every winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由奖杯堆成的山，山脚设着一道小收费站，向每位赢家收费。

examples.en: The court added a penalty for the delay in reporting the accident.
examples.cn: 法院因事故报告延误而加判了一笔处罚。

examples.en: A penalty shoot-out decided the final.
examples.cn: 点球决胜决定了决赛的归属。

examples.en: There is a penalty for paying the loan back early.
examples.cn: 提前还贷是要付违约金的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派人提」——你一犯规，就派人来提走一笔钱 → 罚款、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「处罚、补偿」→ 拉丁形容词 poenalis → 古法语 penalite → 英语 penalty；同族词有 penal、penalize、punitive、punish。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rest on one move: a wrong creates a debt, and the debt is collected. The collection may be a punishment, a sum of money, a statutory sentence, a shot at goal, a golf stroke, a contractual charge, the price of privilege, or a handicap in a race.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立于同一个动作：过错生出一笔债，这笔债要被收回。收回的形式可以是一次处罚、一笔钱、一条法定刑、一脚罚球、一杆罚杆、一项合同收费、特权的代价，或比赛中的不利条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a referee striking one point off the offender's side and moving the other side forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁判从犯规一方的记分上划掉一分，再把另一方往前挪。

branches.en: LEGAL CONSEQUENCE: a fault creates a debt that a verdict or a statute collects in the form of punishment.
branches.cn: 法律后果：过错生出一笔债，由判决或法典以处罚的形式把它收回。

branches.en: MONEY FORM: the debt is counted in coins, from a fine owed to a public authority to a charge written into a contract.
branches.cn: 金钱形式：这笔债用钱币计算，从欠公共机关的一笔罚金到写进合同的一项收费。

branches.en: SPORTING FORM: the payment becomes an uncontested shot at goal or an extra stroke on the card.
branches.cn: 体育形式：这笔代价变成一脚无人防守的射门，或记分卡上多加的一杆。

branches.en: VOLUNTARY PRICE: a privilege or a success brings its own burden, although no rule was broken.
branches.cn: 自愿的代价：特权或成功自带负担，尽管并没有人违规。

branches.en: EQUALIZING BURDEN: a contest lays a disadvantage on the stronger side to level the start.
branches.cn: 平衡的负担：比赛把不利条件加在占优一方，使起跑趋于齐平。

intro.en: Penalty is a noun from the poena family; its Latin adjective and its related verb branch into several English words about punishment.
intro.cn: penalty 是 poena 词族中的名词；它的拉丁形容词与相关动词分出了若干与惩罚有关的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and poenalis give penal, penalty and penalize, while Latin punire, built on poena, gives punish, punishment and punitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与 poenalis 生出 penal、penalty 与 penalize；由 poena 构成的拉丁 punire 则生出 punish、punishment 与 punitive。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of a debt owed after a fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「犯错之后欠下一笔债」的意思。

items.example: The new law raised the penalties for dumping waste.
items.exampleCN: 新法提高了倾倒废弃物的处罚。

items.example: The country still keeps a penal code.
items.exampleCN: 该国仍然保留着一部刑法典。
规则对逾期提交予以处罚。

items.meaning: the act or state of being punished
items.example: He objected to the penalization of small firms.
items.exampleCN: 他反对对小企业施加处罚。

items.example: The measure was more punitive than preventive.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施更偏向惩罚，而非预防。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
the suffering imposed for a wrong
items.meaningCN: 因过错而被施加的痛苦
items.example: The punishment was a month without pay.
Such conduct is punishable by law.
items.exampleCN: 这种行为依法应受处罚。

latinEntries.meaning: to punish; to exact a penalty

definition_zh: 穿透；渗入；洞察；打入（市场）
definition_en: to pass into or through something solid, to spread through a material, to see into something hidden, or to enter a market or group that is hard to reach
core_image: 一根细针顶住表面，慢慢从另一侧露出来
scene: 手术台的灯下，医生把细长的针尖抵住皮肤，缓缓向下推进。The needle penetrated the skin without waking the patient.
sceneCN: 这里是「穿透、刺入」（第 1 个义项：穿过实体屏障）；句意为针头穿过皮肤，病人没有被惊醒。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 penetrate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「穿透；渗透；洞察力」
由现在分词转化而来，义为「有穿透力的；尖锐的」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可被穿透的」
加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「有渗透力的」

senses.title: To pass into or through something solid
senses.definition: to make a way into or through a solid object, often by force or with a sharp point
senses.definitionCN: 进入或穿过坚固物体，常靠外力或尖锐的端点
senses.example: The drill penetrated the concrete wall in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 钻头几秒钟就穿透了混凝土墙。
senses.why: The Latin verb penetrare described going into a body that resists, so the earliest sense is a pointed or forceful entry through a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 penetrare 描述的是进入一个有阻力的物体内部，所以最早的意思是带尖端或靠力量的进入，穿过一道屏障。

senses.title: To spread through a material
senses.definition: to spread through the small spaces of a material, as a liquid, gas or smell does
senses.definitionCN: 像液体、气体或气味那样，通过材料内部的细小空隙扩散开来
senses.example: Smoke had penetrated every room of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 烟已经渗进大楼的每个房间。
senses.why: A liquid or smell does not need one clean hole; it works through tiny gaps, and that slow spreading is the second face of the same entering action.
senses.whyCN: 液体或气味不需要一个整齐的洞，而是从细微的缝隙里钻过去；这种缓慢的扩散，就是「进入」这个动作的第二张面孔。

senses.title: To see into something hidden
senses.definition: to see through a disguise, a plan or a mystery and understand what is really there
senses.definitionCN: 看穿伪装、计划或谜团，理解其中真正的东西
senses.example: Her calm questions penetrated his carefully built excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的追问看穿了他精心编造的借口。
senses.why: English treats sight as something that reaches inside a thing, so the verb of going through a wall becomes the verb of going through a lie.
senses.whyCN: 英语把目光看成能伸进事物内部的东西，于是「穿墙」的动词也成了「看穿谎言」的动词。

senses.title: To enter a market or a closed group
senses.definition: to get into a market, an organization or a group that outsiders find hard to reach
senses.definitionCN: 进入外人难以触及的市场、机构或群体
senses.example: The brand took ten years to penetrate the local market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌花了十年才打入当地市场。
senses.why: A market or a club is imagined as a closed body with a wall around it, so getting inside is pictured as the same act of pushing through.
senses.whyCN: 市场和圈子被想象成有围墙的封闭身体，于是「进去」就被画成同一个往里挤的动作。

intro.en: Penetrate comes straight from Latin, where a word for the inner part of a house grew into a verb for going inside anything.
intro.cn: penetrate 直接来自拉丁语：一个表示房屋最里侧的词，长成了表示「进入任何东西内部」的动词。

items.en: Penus named the inner store of a house, the part where food and valuables were kept; the link to the verb is generally accepted but not certain.
items.cn: penus 指房屋最里侧的储藏处，存放食物和贵重物品的地方；它与动词的联系一般认为成立，但并非定论。

items.en: The adverb penitus meant inward, deep inside, and it supplied the picture of a point moving toward the middle.
items.cn: 副词 penitus 意为向内、在深处，提供了「一个点朝中心移动」的画面。

items.en: Penetrare meant to enter, pierce or pass through, and Roman writers used it for armies, weapons and even arguments.
items.cn: penetrare 意为进入、刺穿、穿过，罗马作家用它写军队、武器，甚至写论证。

items.en: English borrowed the verb directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, first for physical piercing and soon for understanding.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个动词，先指身体上的刺穿，很快又用于理解。

items.en: Modern English uses it for liquids in walls, ideas in minds and products in markets, all as versions of one act.
items.cn: 现代英语用它说墙里的液体、脑子里的观念、市场上的产品，全都是同一个动作的不同版本。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects verbs of piercing, seeping and getting inside.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示刺入、渗出与进入内部的动词。

entries.definition: The act of passing into or through something, or the ability to see deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 穿入或穿过的动作，也指看得很深的能力。

entries.definition: Able to pass through, or sharp and full of insight.
entries.definitionCN: 能穿过的；尖锐而有洞察力的。

entries.definition: Possible to pass through or get into.
entries.definitionCN: 可被穿过或进入的。

entries.definition: Having the power to pass into something deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 具有深入穿透力的。

entries.definition: To make a hole in something with a sharp point.
entries.definitionCN: 用尖物在某物上扎出孔。

entries.definition: To flow slowly through small openings.
entries.definitionCN: 从细小开口缓慢流出或渗入。

entries.definition: To spread through every part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 扩散到某物的每个部分。

entries.definition: To enter an organization or place secretly.
entries.definitionCN: 秘密进入某个组织或地方。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for the inner part, and its family keeps returning to the act of getting inside something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「最里侧」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到「进入内部」这个动作。

normal.en: Penitus in Latin means deep inside, and penetrate still carries that inward direction.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 penitus 意为「在深处」，penetrate 至今保留着这个向内的方向。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks a Latin verb, so penetrate behaves like a doing word, not a naming word.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 是拉丁动词的标志，所以 penetrate 是「做」的词，不是「命名」的词。

normal.en: Add -ion and you get penetration, the act itself; add -ing and you get the quality of getting through.
normal.cn: 加 -ion 得到 penetration，指动作本身；加 -ing 得到「能穿过去」的性质。

normal.en: Pierce is a single sharp hole, while penetrate can also mean spreading through a whole material.
normal.cn: pierce 是一个尖锐的孔，penetrate 还能表示浸透整块材料。

normal.en: A company that penetrates a market is doing to the market what a needle does to cloth.
normal.cn: 企业「打入市场」，对市场做的正是针对于布做的事。

abstract.en: To penetrate is to refuse to stop at the surface, whether the surface is a wall, a rumour or a face.
abstract.cn: 穿透就是不肯停在表面，不管表面是墙、是传言，还是一张脸。

abstract.en: The same word covers a needle, a smell and an argument because all three leave the outside and reach the inside.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能覆盖针、气味和论证，因为这三者都离开外部、抵达内部。

abstract.en: A market is treated as a body with skin, which is why selling is described with the language of surgery.
abstract.cn: 市场被当成有皮肤的身体，所以销售也用外科手术的语言来描述。

examples.en: The arrow penetrated the wooden shield and stuck fast.
examples.cn: 箭穿透木盾，牢牢钉住。

examples.en: Cold air penetrated the thin walls of the hut.
examples.cn: 冷空气渗进小屋薄薄的墙。

examples.en: Few reporters have penetrated the secretive world of the firm.
examples.cn: 很少有记者能进入这家公司隐秘的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮内戳的」——针尖戳进皮肉里面，就是穿透；记住 penetrate。

root: 拉丁语 penus（房屋最里侧的储藏处）经副词 penitus（向内、在深处）发展出动词 penetrare（进入、穿透）；英语十六世纪直接借入，同族词多与「进入内部」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core act is getting inside; the senses differ only in what is being entered, a solid object, a material, a hidden truth or a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是「进入内部」；各义项的差别只在进入的是什么——固体、材料、隐情，还是市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine needle pressing on a surface and showing up on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细针压住表面，从另一侧露出来。

branches.en: a needle sliding through leather
branches.cn: 针穿过皮革

branches.en: rain working its way through roof tiles
branches.cn: 雨水从瓦片间渗下去

branches.en: a stare that strips away an excuse
branches.cn: 一眼看掉借口

branches.en: a brand pushing into a guarded market
branches.cn: 品牌挤进被守住的市场

branches.en: from breaking a surface to breaking a lie
branches.cn: 从破开表面到破开谎言

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin adverb for the inner part, its verb of entering, and a set of Latin and English endings that turn it into a noun and qualities.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语中表示「里侧」的副词、表示「进入」的动词，以及一组把它变成名词和性质词的拉丁、英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on penitus, inward, and the verb penetrare, to enter; the noun penetratio names the act.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 penitus（向内）与动词 penetrare（进入）之上；名词 penetratio 表示进入这一动作。

items.meaning: act or result of an action

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：具有做……的性质

definition_zh: 养老金；退休金；津贴；发给…养老金
definition_en: a regular sum paid to someone who has stopped working, a similar allowance for other reasons, or to give such a payment to someone
core_image: 一只按月寄到的信封，装着固定的生活费
scene: 厂里的老会计到了退休年纪，人事把一份表格推到他面前。After forty years, he was pensioned off with a modest monthly income.
sceneCN: 这里是「发给…养老金、使退休」（第 3 个义项：动词用法）；句意为干了四十年后，他领着一笔不多的月钱被安排退休。

derivatives.zh: 由 pension 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「领养老金的人」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「有资格领取养老金的」
加后缀 -ary 构成，义为「养老金的；领取养老金的」

senses.title: Regular income after retirement
senses.definition: a sum of money paid regularly to a person who has retired from work
senses.definitionCN: 定期支付给已退休人员的钱
senses.example: She lives on a small state pension.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠一笔不多的国家养老金生活。
senses.why: Latin pensio began as a payment weighed out on a fixed measure, and that fixed measure is what makes the modern payment regular rather than earned hour by hour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pensio 最初指按固定份量称出来的付款，正是这种「固定份量」让今天的这笔钱按月发放，而不是按小时挣来。

senses.title: A similar allowance for other reasons
senses.definition: a regular payment made for injury, widowhood or long service rather than for retirement
senses.definitionCN: 因伤残、丧偶或长期服务而定期领取的钱，而不是因为退休
senses.example: The widow receives a pension from the state.
senses.exampleCN: 这位遗孀从国家领取抚恤金。
senses.why: Once the word meant a periodic payment rather than a wage, it could cover any fixed allowance, because the timing, not the reason, defines it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指的不是工资而是定期付款，它就能覆盖任何固定补助，因为定义它的是发放的节奏，而不是发放的理由。

senses.title: To give someone a pension and end their work
senses.definition: to pay a pension to someone, usually when their working life is being brought to an end
senses.definitionCN: 向某人支付养老金，通常是在结束其职业生涯的时候
senses.example: The firm pensioned off three senior managers last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年公司让三位高级经理领养老金退休了。
senses.why: The verb turns the payment into an act done to a person; the particle off adds the sense of being set aside from the active staff.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「付款」变成对某人做的动作；小品词 off 又添上「被从在职人员中挪开」的意思。

intro.en: Pension goes back to a Latin verb for hanging and weighing, whose noun came to mean a payment measured out at a fixed time.
intro.cn: pension 可上溯到拉丁语中表示悬挂与称重的动词，其名词后来指在固定时间量出来的付款。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang and also to weigh and pay out, because goods were weighed against metal on a balance.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂，也表示称重和付款，因为货物要在天平上与金属对量。

items.en: Pensio named a weighing and then a payment, the sum measured out at an agreed time.
items.cn: pensio 先指称量，后指付款，即在约定时间称量出来的那笔钱。

items.en: Old French took pension as a payment or rent and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把 pension 用作付款或租金，并在诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English pension meant a fixed regular payment, often for service or favour.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pension 指固定定期付款，常因服务或恩惠而给。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the main sense to retirement income and grew a verb meaning to retire someone on such pay.
items.cn: 现代英语把主要义项收窄为退休收入，并长出「发养老金使某人退休」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the derived forms and other words on the Latin stem for hanging and weighing; the near-meaning group collects kinds of regular payment.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同一拉丁词干（悬挂、称重）上的其他词；近义组收各类定期付款。

entries.definition: A person who receives a pension.
entries.definitionCN: 领取养老金的人。

entries.definition: Giving the right to receive a pension.
entries.definitionCN: 有资格领取养老金的。

entries.definition: To hang something up, or to stop it for a time.
entries.definitionCN: 悬挂；暂停。

entries.definition: A piece of jewellery that hangs from a chain.
entries.definitionCN: 挂在链子上的吊坠。

entries.definition: Money paid regularly for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的定期支付的钱。

entries.definition: A fixed sum paid every year, often for life.
entries.definitionCN: 每年支付的固定金额，常为终身。

entries.definition: Money paid by the state to people in need.
entries.definitionCN: 国家发给困难者的补助。

entries.definition: British term for a retirement pension scheme.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指退休养老金制度。

normalIntro.en: The word hangs on a Latin verb for weighing and paying, and its family keeps the picture of a sum measured out at fixed times.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词挂在拉丁语表示称重与付款的动词上，同族词保留着「按固定时间量出一笔钱」的画面。

normal.en: Pendere means to weigh, so a pension is money that was once weighed out on a balance.
normal.cn: pendere 意为称重，所以养老金最初是天平上称出来的钱。

normal.en: Suspend and pendant share the same root: to hang, which is what a balance does before it settles.
normal.cn: suspend 与 pendant 同根，都是「悬挂」，这正是天平在稳定前的动作。

normal.en: Add -er and a pensioner is the person on the receiving end of the payment.
normal.cn: 加 -er，pensioner 就是收这笔钱的人。

normal.en: Pension off means to move someone onto a pension and out of the active list.
normal.cn: pension off 意为把某人转到养老金上、移出在职名单。

normal.en: Pension is the income; allowance is the wider word for any regular payment.
normal.cn: pension 是这笔收入本身；allowance 是更宽的词，指任何定期付款。

abstract.en: A pension is time turned into money: years of work are weighed and paid back month by month.
abstract.cn: 养老金是把时间换成了钱：多年的工作被称量，再按月还回来。

abstract.en: The word remembers a balance because retirement is an accounting of a whole working life.
abstract.cn: 这个词记着一架天平，因为退休是对一整段职业生涯的结算。

abstract.en: To be pensioned off is to be valued and set aside at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 被安排领养老金退休，是在同一刻既被计价、又被挪到一边。

examples.en: She lives on a small state pension.
examples.cn: 她靠一笔不多的国家养老金生活。

examples.en: The firm pensioned off three senior managers last year.
examples.cn: 去年公司让三位高级经理领养老金退休了。

examples.en: His pension is paid directly into the bank.
examples.cn: 他的养老金直接打进银行账户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盼薪」——退休以后每个月盼着那笔薪水到账；记住 pension 是养老金。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称重、付款）派生名词 pensio（称量、付款），经古法语 pension 进入英语；同族词多与「悬挂、称量」有关。

sensesIntro.en: One core payment, measured out at fixed times, divides into retirement income, other allowances, and the act of putting someone on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一笔按固定时间量出来的钱，分成退休收入、其他补助，以及「让某人领这笔钱」的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an envelope arriving every month with a fixed sum inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只按月寄到的信封，装着固定的生活费。

branches.en: a monthly payment after the last day at work
branches.cn: 最后一个工作日之后的月付

branches.en: a payment for injury or widowhood
branches.cn: 因伤残或丧偶而领的钱

branches.en: a manager being moved onto the retired list
branches.cn: 经理被转到退休名单

branches.en: from receiving the money to being retired on it
branches.cn: 从领这笔钱到因它而退休

branches.en: the same payment seen as income and as an action
branches.cn: 同一笔钱作为收入和作为动作

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb of weighing and paying, its noun, and English endings that name the person and the right.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示称重与付款的动词、它的名词，以及把人、把资格命名出来的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family hangs on pendere, to hang and to weigh, and its noun pensio, a payment measured out; English took the noun through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族挂在 pendere（悬挂、称重）与名词 pensio（量出来的付款）上；英语经法语借入的是名词。

items.meaning: to hang, to weigh, to pay
act or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词词尾：动作或其结果

items.meaning: a person who receives a pension

items.meaningCN: 后缀：做某事或接受某事的人

items.meaning: that can be or is entitled to

definition_zh: 胡椒；胡椒粉；辣椒；撒胡椒粉
definition_en: a hot spice made from dried berries, the hollow fruit of related plants used as a vegetable, or to scatter this spice over food
core_image: 手指捻动小瓶，深色粉末簌簌落在食物上
scene: 灶台前，厨师把刚煎好的牛排放在案板上，手腕一抖，细粉落满表面。The chef peppered the steak and slid it onto the plate.
sceneCN: 这里是「撒胡椒粉」（第 3 个义项：动词用法）；句意为厨师给牛排撒上胡椒，再把它滑进盘子。

derivatives.zh: 由 pepper 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「胡椒味的；辛辣的；脾气急的」
由 pepper 与 corn 复合而成，义为「胡椒粒」
由 pepper 与 mint 复合而成，指薄荷，因味道刺激而得名
由 pepper 与 mill 复合而成，义为「胡椒研磨器」

senses.title: The spice made from dried berries
senses.definition: a hot spice made from the dried berries of a tropical vine, used as a powder or in whole grains
senses.definitionCN: 由热带藤本植物的干果制成的辛辣香料，可磨成粉或整粒使用
senses.example: Season the soup with salt and freshly ground pepper.
senses.exampleCN: 用盐和现磨的胡椒给汤调味。
senses.why: Latin piper named the spice itself, and English kept it as a mass noun for the powder that is shaken over food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 piper 指的就是这种香料本身，英语把它保留为不可数名词，指撒在食物上的粉末。

senses.title: The hollow fruit eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: the hollow fruit of plants in the same family, eaten as a vegetable in colours such as green, red and yellow
senses.definitionCN: 同科植物的中空果实，作为蔬菜食用，有绿、红、黄等颜色
senses.example: She stuffed the peppers with rice and baked them.
senses.exampleCN: 她把米饭塞进辣椒里烤熟。
senses.why: The spice and the vegetable come from the same plant family, so one name covers both, and cooks count the vegetable one by one.
senses.whyCN: 香料和蔬菜来自同一科植物，于是一个名称覆盖两者；而做菜时蔬菜是一颗颗数的。

senses.title: To scatter pepper over food
senses.definition: to shake pepper or a similar powder over food before eating or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 在烹调或进食前把胡椒或类似粉末撒在食物上
senses.example: He peppered the eggs and handed me the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 他给鸡蛋撒上胡椒，把盘子递给我。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: the powder leaves the shaker in small specks and lands on whatever lies below.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词动起来：粉末从瓶里成小点落下，落在下面的东西上。

senses.title: To cover with many small things
senses.definition: to cover a surface with many small marks or objects, or to hit someone with a rapid stream of questions, shots or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 用许多小点或小物布满一个表面，或向某人连续发出问题、射击或批评
senses.example: Reporters peppered her with questions as she left the court.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开法庭时，记者们连珠炮般向她提问。
senses.why: Once pepper is a shower of specks, the verb can describe anything arriving that way, so words and bullets behave like grains of powder.
senses.whyCN: 一旦胡椒被看成一阵密集的小点，这个动词就能描写任何以这种方式到来的东西，于是话语和子弹都像粉末颗粒。

intro.en: Pepper travelled west along trade routes, from an Indic name for long pepper through Greek and Latin into Old English.
intro.cn: pepper 沿着贸易路线西行，从印度方面表示长胡椒的名称，经希腊语、拉丁语进入古英语。

items.en: Sanskrit pippali named long pepper, and the deeper origin of the word is generally thought to lie outside Indo-European, possibly in a Dravidian language.
items.cn: 梵语 pippali 指长胡椒，这个词更早的来源一般认为在印欧语之外，可能来自某种达罗毗荼语。

items.en: Greek took the word as peperi, and Greek traders carried both the spice and the name westward.
items.cn: 希腊语把它写作 peperi，希腊商人把香料和名称一起带向西方。

items.en: Latin piper named the spice, and Roman cooks used it so heavily that it became a common item of trade.
items.cn: 拉丁语 piper 指胡椒，罗马厨师用得极多，使它成了常见的贸易货品。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin word as pipor, and the spelling later shifted to pepper.
items.cn: 古英语借入拉丁词写作 pipor，后来拼写演变为 pepper。

items.en: Modern English keeps the spice and the vegetable under one word and uses the verb for any dense shower of things.
items.cn: 现代英语用同一个词表示香料和蔬菜，并用动词描写任何密集袭来的一阵东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derived words and compounds built on the spice name; the near-meaning group collects other seasonings and members of the pepper family.
note.cn: 形近组收由这一香料名构成的派生词与复合词；近义组收其他调味料以及胡椒家族的成员。

entries.definition: Tasting of pepper, or quick to anger.
entries.definitionCN: 有胡椒味的；易怒的。

entries.definition: A single dried berry of the pepper plant.
entries.definitionCN: 胡椒的整粒干果。

entries.definition: A small device for grinding peppercorns.
entries.definitionCN: 研磨胡椒粒的小器具。

entries.definition: A mint plant with a strong cool taste.
entries.definitionCN: 一种薄荷，名字取自胡椒般的刺激味道，与胡椒并非同一种植物。

entries.definition: A small hot pepper used in cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 做菜用的小而辣的辣椒。

entries.definition: A dried plant substance used to flavour food.
entries.definitionCN: 用于给食物调味的干燥植物性香料。

entries.definition: The botanical name for peppers and their fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 辣椒属及其果实的植物学名称。

entries.definition: Salt, pepper or spices added to improve flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 为提味而加的盐、胡椒或香料。

normalIntro.en: The word keeps a Latin spice name on top of an older Indic root, and its family stays close to the kitchen and to the idea of many small specks.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在更古老的印度词根之上保存了一个拉丁香料名，同族词始终贴近厨房，也贴近「许多小颗粒」这个意象。

normal.en: Piper is the Latin name, and the English word keeps the double p of the original.
normal.cn: piper 是拉丁名，英语词保留了原词的双写 p。

normal.en: The spice is uncountable, so you say some pepper, while the vegetable is countable, so you say two peppers.
normal.cn: 香料不可数，说 some pepper；蔬菜可数，说 two peppers。

normal.en: Peppery adds -y, the suffix that turns a noun into a quality, so the word means full of pepper.
normal.cn: peppery 加 -y，这个后缀把名词变成性质，所以词义是「充满胡椒的」。

normal.en: A peppercorn is one grain, which is why a mill grinds corns rather than powder.
normal.cn: peppercorn 是一粒，所以研磨器磨的是颗粒而不是粉末。

normal.en: Pepper with questions borrows the picture of many small grains hitting a surface at once.
normal.cn: pepper with questions 借用了许多小颗粒同时打在一个表面上的画面。

abstract.en: A spice and a vegetable share one name because both come from the same family, and language often prefers the family resemblance over precision.
abstract.cn: 香料和蔬菜共用一个名字，因为两者同科；语言常常更看重亲缘相似，而不是精确区分。

abstract.en: To pepper someone with questions is to treat words as if they were grains thrown by the handful.
abstract.cn: 用问题 pepper 某人，就是把话语当成一把把撒出去的颗粒。

abstract.en: The word travelled from a Sanskrit name for long pepper to a Latin trade good to an English kitchen, carried by the same appetite.
abstract.cn: 这个词从梵语的长胡椒之名，走到拉丁语的贸易货，再走到英语的厨房，靠的是同一种胃口。

examples.en: Season the soup with salt and freshly ground pepper.
examples.cn: 用盐和现磨的胡椒给汤调味。

examples.en: The garden is full of green and red peppers.
examples.cn: 园子里长满了青椒和红椒。

examples.en: Journalists peppered her with questions as she left the court.
examples.cn: 她离开法庭时，记者们连珠炮般向她提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍拍」——往牛排上拍拍胡椒瓶，粉末落下来；记住 pepper 是胡椒。

sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指香料、同科的蔬菜、撒粉的动作，以及任何密集落下的小东西。
